title.zh: 卷一百九十七 列傳第一百四十七: 南蠻 西南蠻
title.en: Volume 197 Biographies 147: Southern Man, Southernwest Man
title.raw: 卷一百九十七 列傳第一百四十七: 南蠻 西南蠻 Volume 197 Biographies 147: Southern Man, Southernwest Man

sentences.zh: 林邑國，漢日南象林之地，在交州南千餘里。

translations.literal: The state of Linyi was in Han the land of Xianglin in Rinan, more than a thousand li south of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Linyi occupied the Han-era Xianglin district of Rinan commandery, lying more than a thousand li south of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 其國延袤數千里，北與皛州接。

translations.literal: Its state extends several thousand li; on the north it borders Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The realm stretches several thousand li from end to end and shares a northern border with Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 地氣冬溫，不識冰雪，常多霧雨。

translations.literal: The climate of the land is warm in winter; they know neither ice nor snow, and there are constantly many fogs and rains.
translations.idiomatic: Winters are mild there; ice and snow are unknown, and fog and rain are frequent throughout the year.

sentences.zh: 其王所居城，立木為柵。

translations.literal: The city where the king dwells has a palisade of standing timbers.
translations.idiomatic: The king's capital is ringed by a stockade of upright timbers.

sentences.zh: 王著日氈古貝，斜絡膊，繞腰，上加真珠金鎖，以為瓔珞，卷發而戴花。

translations.literal: The king wears sun-felt kapok cloth, a slanting net on the arms, wrapped about the waist, with pearls and gold chains above, made into a necklace; curled hair and wearing flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The king dresses in sun-bleached kapok cloth, with a crossed net on his arms and a sash about his waist, pearls and gold chains worked into a necklace, his hair in curls and adorned with flowers.

sentences.zh: 夫人服朝霞古貝以為短裙，首戴金花，身飾以金鎖真珠瓔珞。

translations.literal: The lady wears dawn-glow kapok cloth as a short skirt, on the head wears golden flowers, the body adorned with gold chains and pearl necklaces.
translations.idiomatic: The queen wears dawn-colored kapok cloth as a short skirt, golden flowers in her hair, and gold chains and pearl necklaces on her person.

sentences.zh: 王之侍衛，有兵五千人，能用弩及，以藤為甲，以竹為弓，乘象而戰。

translations.literal: The king's bodyguard has five thousand troops, able to use crossbows and spears; they take rattan for armor, bamboo for bows, and ride elephants to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The king's guard numbers five thousand men skilled with crossbows and spears; they wear rattan armor, shoot bamboo bows, and go into battle mounted on elephants.

sentences.zh: 王出則列象千頭，馬四百匹，分為前後。

translations.literal: When the king goes out, a thousand elephants are arrayed and four hundred horses, divided into front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the king goes abroad, a thousand elephants and four hundred horses are drawn up in front and rear formations.

sentences.zh: 其人拳發色黑，俗皆徒跣，得麝香以塗身，一日之中，再塗再洗。

translations.literal: Its people have curly hair and black color; customarily all go barefoot; obtaining musk they smear the body, and within one day they smear and wash twice.
translations.idiomatic: The people have curly black hair and ordinarily go barefoot; they obtain musk to rub on their bodies, applying and washing it off twice in the course of a single day.

sentences.zh: 拜謁皆合掌頓顙。

translations.literal: In paying respects all press palms together and bow the forehead.
translations.idiomatic: When paying respects they always press their palms together and bow their foreheads to the ground.

sentences.zh: 嫁娶之法，得取同姓。

translations.literal: The law of marriage: one may take a person of the same surname.
translations.idiomatic: In marriage custom, men may wed women of the same clan name.

sentences.zh: 俗有文字，尤信佛法，人多出家。

translations.literal: The custom has writing; they especially believe in the Buddhist Law; many people leave the household.
translations.idiomatic: They have a written script and are especially devoted to Buddhism; many take monastic vows.

sentences.zh: 父母死，子則剔發而哭，以棺盛屍，積柴燔柩，收其灰，藏於金瓶，送之水中。

translations.literal: When parents die, sons then shave the head and weep, place the corpse in a coffin, pile firewood and burn the bier, gather the ashes, store them in a golden jar, and send them into the water.
translations.idiomatic: When parents die, their sons shave their heads and mourn; the body is placed in a coffin, heaped with firewood and cremated, the ashes collected in a gold urn, and committed to the water.

sentences.zh: 俗以十二月為歲首，稻歲再熟。

translations.literal: Custom takes the twelfth month as the year's head; rice ripens twice a year.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth month is reckoned the start of the year, and rice is harvested twice annually.

sentences.zh: 自此以南，草木冬榮，四時皆食生菜，以檳榔汁為酒。

translations.literal: From here southward, grass and trees flourish in winter; in all four seasons they eat raw vegetables, and take areca juice as wine.
translations.idiomatic: South of this region plants stay green through winter; raw vegetables are eaten in every season, and areca juice serves as wine.

sentences.zh: 有結遼鳥，能解人語。

translations.literal: There is a jieliao bird able to understand human speech.
translations.idiomatic: There is a jieliao bird that can understand human language.

sentences.zh: 武德六年，其王範梵誌遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude, its king Fan Fanzhi sent envoys to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wude (623), King Fan Fanzhi of Linyi sent envoys to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 八年，又遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, again they sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later they again sent tribute of local products.

sentences.zh: 高祖為設《九部樂》以宴之，及賜其王錦彩。

translations.literal: Gaozu had the Nine Department Music performed to feast them, and bestowed on their king brocades.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu entertained them with the Nine Department Music and granted their king silks and brocades.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遣使貢馴犀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, they sent envoys presenting tribute of tame rhinoceroses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era they sent envoys offering tame rhinoceroses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年，其王範頭黎遣使獻火珠，大如雞卵，圓白皎潔，光照數尺，狀如水精，正午向日。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, its king Fan Touli sent envoys presenting a fire pearl, large as a hen's egg, round, white, bright and clean, its light shining several feet, shaped like rock crystal; at noon facing the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan (630), King Fan Touli sent envoys with a fire pearl the size of a hen's egg—round, white, and lustrous, casting light for several feet and resembling crystal; held toward the sun at noon,

sentences.zh: 以艾蒸之，即火燃。

translations.literal: when moxa is steamed against it, fire immediately blazes.
translations.idiomatic: it would ignite when heated with burning moxa.

sentences.zh: 五年，又獻五色鸚鵡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, again they presented a five-colored parrot.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they presented a multicolored parrot.

sentences.zh: 太宗異之，詔太子右庶子李百藥為之賦。

translations.literal: Taizong marveled at it and ordered the Right Vice Censor of the Heir Apparent Li Baiyao to compose a rhapsody on it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was astonished and ordered Li Baiyao, right vice censor of the heir apparent, to compose a rhapsody in its honor.

sentences.zh: 又獻白鸚鵡，精識辯慧，善於應答。

translations.literal: Again they presented a white parrot, keen in perception, eloquent and clever, skilled in replying.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent a white parrot of keen wit and ready speech, adept at conversation.

sentences.zh: 太宗憫之，並付其使，令放還於林藪。

translations.literal: Taizong pitied them and handed both to their envoys, ordering them released back to the forest groves.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong took pity on the birds and returned both to the envoys with orders to release them in the wild.

sentences.zh: 自此朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: From this time tribute missions did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: From that time forward their tribute missions never ceased.

sentences.zh: 頭黎死，子範鎮龍代立。

translations.literal: Touli died; his son Fan Zhenlong succeeded in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Touli died, his son Fan Zhenlong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，詔於陵所刊石圖頭黎之形，列於玄闕之前。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, an edict ordered at the mausoleum site carved stone images of Touli's form, arrayed before the Dark Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's death, an edict directed that carved stone images of Touli be set before the Dark Gate of the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 十九年，鎮龍為其臣摩訶漫多伽獨所殺，其宗族並誅夷，範氏遂絕。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Zhenlong was killed by his minister Mohe Manduojia; his clan was all exterminated and executed, and the Fan house thus ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Zhenguan (645), Zhenlong was murdered by his minister Mohe Manduojia; the entire Fan clan was put to death, and the royal line came to an end.

sentences.zh: 國人乃立頭黎之女婿婆羅門為王。

translations.literal: The people of the state then installed Touli's son-in-law Boluomen as king.
translations.idiomatic: The people thereupon enthroned Touli's son-in-law Boluomen as king.

sentences.zh: 後大臣及國人感思舊主。

translations.literal: Later the great ministers and the people of the state were moved to think of the former lord.
translations.idiomatic: Later the chief ministers and the populace, moved by longing for their former ruler,

sentences.zh: 乃廢婆羅門而立頭黎之嫡女為王。

translations.literal: then deposed Boluomen and installed Touli's eldest daughter by the principal wife as king.
translations.idiomatic: deposed Boluomen and made Touli's daughter by his principal wife their queen.

sentences.zh: 自林邑以南，皆卷髮黑身，通號為「昆侖」。

translations.literal: From Linyi southward, all have curled hair and black bodies, and are commonly called "Kunlun."
translations.idiomatic: South of Linyi the peoples all have curly hair and dark skin and are collectively known as Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 婆利國，在林邑東南海中洲上。

translations.literal: The state of Poli is on an islet in the southeastern sea from Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Poli lies on an island in the sea southeast of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 其地延袤數千里，自交州南渡海，經林邑、扶南、赤土、丹丹數國乃至焉。

translations.literal: Its territory extends several thousand li; from Jiaozhou crossing the sea southward, passing Linyi, Funan, Chitu, Dandan, and several states, one then arrives there.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory runs several thousand li; from Jiaozhou one crosses the southern sea, passing Linyi, Funan, Chitu, Dandan, and other kingdoms before reaching it.

sentences.zh: 其人皆黑色，穿耳附榼。

translations.literal: Its people are all black in color; they pierce the ears and attach wooden plugs.
translations.idiomatic: The inhabitants are all dark-skinned and wear wooden plugs in pierced ears.

sentences.zh: 王姓剎利耶伽，名護路那婆，世有其位。

translations.literal: The king's surname is Ksatriyayaka; his name is Hulunaba; the position is hereditary in the family.
translations.idiomatic: The royal line bears the surname Ksatriyayaka; the reigning name is Hulunaba, and the throne passes in succession within the family.

sentences.zh: 王戴花形如皮弁，裝以真珠瓔珞，身坐金床。

translations.literal: The king wears a flowered cap shaped like a leather cap, adorned with pearl necklaces; the body sits on a golden couch.
translations.idiomatic: The king wears a flowered cap in the shape of a court cap, strung with pearl necklaces, and sits upon a golden couch.

sentences.zh: 侍女有金花寶縷之飾，或持白拂孔雀扇。

translations.literal: Serving women have ornaments of golden flowers and jeweled threads, or hold white whisks and peacock fans.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant women wear ornaments of golden flowers and jeweled threads, and some carry white whisks or peacock-feather fans.

sentences.zh: 行則駕象，鳴金擊鼓吹蠡為樂。

translations.literal: When traveling they drive elephants; sounding metal and striking drums, blowing conches as music.
translations.idiomatic: When the king travels he rides elephants, while gongs, drums, and conch horns provide music.

sentences.zh: 男子皆拳發，被古貝，布橫幅以繞腰。

translations.literal: Men all have curly hair, wear kapok cloth, and wrap a horizontal cloth strip about the waist.
translations.idiomatic: The men all have curly hair, wear kapok-cloth garments, and wind a broad strip of cloth about the waist.

sentences.zh: 風氣暑熱，恆如中國之盛夏。

translations.literal: Wind and climate are sweltering hot, constantly like midsummer in China.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is torrid year-round, as sultry as a Chinese midsummer.

sentences.zh: 谷一歲再熟。

translations.literal: Grain ripens twice in one year.
translations.idiomatic: Grain is harvested twice a year.

sentences.zh: 有古貝草，緝其花以作布，粗者名古貝，細者名白赩。

translations.literal: There is kapok grass; they weave its flowers to make cloth—the coarse called kapok cloth, the fine called white xi.
translations.idiomatic: Kapok is cultivated; its blossoms are woven into cloth—the coarse grade called kapok cloth, the fine called white xi.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，其王遣使隨林邑使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, its king sent envoys following Linyi's envoys to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan (630) its king sent envoys in the train of Linyi's mission with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 盤盤國，在林邑西南海曲中，北與林邑隔小海，自交州船行四十日乃至，其國與狼牙修國為鄰，人皆學婆羅門書，甚敬佛法。

translations.literal: The state of Panpan is in the bend of the southwestern sea from Linyi; on the north it is separated from Linyi by a small sea; from Jiaozhou by ship forty days then arriving; its state borders the state of Langyaxiu; people all study Brahmanical writing and greatly revere the Buddhist Law.
translations.idiomatic: Panpan lies in a bay of the sea southwest of Linyi, separated from Linyi on the north by a narrow strait; from Jiaozhou it is forty days' sail. It borders Langyaxiu; the people study Brahmanical script and are deeply devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，遣使來朝，貢方物。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, they sent envoys to come to court and presented local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan (635) they sent envoys to court bearing local tribute.

sentences.zh: 貞臘國，在林邑西北，本扶南之屬國，「昆侖」之類。

translations.literal: The state of Zhenla is northwest of Linyi; originally a subject state of Funan, of the Kunlun type.
translations.idiomatic: Chenla lies northwest of Linyi; formerly a dependency of Funan, it belongs to the Kunlun peoples.

sentences.zh: 在京師南二萬七百里，北至愛州六十日行。

translations.literal: From the capital south twenty-seven thousand li; north to Aizhou sixty days' travel.
translations.idiomatic: It stands twenty-seven thousand li south of the capital; from its northern border to Aizhou is a journey of sixty days.

sentences.zh: 其王姓剎利氏。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is the Ksatriya clan.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house bears the Ksatriya surname.

sentences.zh: 有大城三十余所，王都伊奢那城，風俗被服與林邑同。

translations.literal: There are more than thirty great cities; the royal capital is Yishena city; customs of dress and clothing are the same as Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: It has more than thirty major cities; the capital is Yishena, and dress and custom match those of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 地饒瘴癘毒。

translations.literal: The land abounds in miasmal pestilence and poison.
translations.idiomatic: The country is rife with malarial miasma and pestilence.

sentences.zh: 海中大魚有時半出，望之如山。

translations.literal: Great fish in the sea sometimes half emerge; gazing at them they seem like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Enormous sea creatures sometimes surface halfway, looming like mountains on the horizon.

sentences.zh: 每五六月中，毒氣流行，即以牛豕祠之，不者則五谷不登。

translations.literal: Every year in the fifth and sixth months, poisonous vapors spread; then they sacrifice cattle and pigs to them; if not, the five grains do not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: Each year between the fifth and sixth months poisonous vapors prevail, and cattle and pigs are sacrificed to them—otherwise the harvest fails.

sentences.zh: 其俗東向開戶，以東為上。

translations.literal: Their custom opens doors facing east; they take the east as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Their custom is to open doorways to the east and regard the east as the place of honor.

sentences.zh: 有戰象五千頭，尤好者飼以飯肉。

translations.literal: There are five thousand war elephants; the especially favored are fed with rice and meat.
translations.idiomatic: They maintain five thousand war elephants, the finest of which are fed on grain and meat.

sentences.zh: 與鄰國戰，則象隊在前，於背上以木作樓，上有四人，皆持弓箭。

translations.literal: When fighting neighboring states, the elephant corps goes in front; on their backs they make towers of wood, with four men above, all holding bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In war with neighboring states the elephant corps leads; wooden towers are built on their backs, each manned by four archers.

sentences.zh: 國尚佛道及天神，天神為大，佛道次之。

translations.literal: The state esteems the Buddhist Way and the Heavenly Spirit; the Heavenly Spirit is greater, the Buddhist Way second.
translations.idiomatic: The realm honors both the Buddhist faith and the heavenly spirits, with the heavenly spirits taking precedence and Buddhism second.

sentences.zh: 武德六年，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wude, they sent envoys presenting local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wude (623) they sent envoys with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，又與林邑國俱來朝獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, again together with the state of Linyi they came to court with offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan (628) they came to court jointly with Linyi.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉其陸海疲勞，錫賚甚厚。

translations.literal: Taizong commended their fatigue over land and sea and bestowed gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised their arduous journey by land and sea and rewarded them most generously.

sentences.zh: 南方人謂真臘國為吉蔑國。

translations.literal: Southerners call the state of Zhenla the state of Jimie.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners refer to Chenla as Jimie.

sentences.zh: 自神龍以後，真臘分為二半：以南近海多陂澤處，謂之水真臘半；

translations.literal: From Shenlong onward, Zhenla was divided into two halves: the part south near the sea with many marshes and pools, called the half of Water Zhenla;
translations.idiomatic: After the Shenlong era Chenla split in two: the southern portion near the sea with its many marshes and lagoons was called Water Chenla;

sentences.zh: 以北多山阜，謂之陸真臘，亦謂之文單國。

translations.literal: that to the north with many hills and mounds, called Land Zhenla, also called the state of Wendan.
translations.idiomatic: the northern portion of hills and uplands was called Land Chenla, also known as Wendan.

sentences.zh: 高宗、則天、玄宗朝，並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Gaozong, Zetian, and Xuanzong, all sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, Empress Wu, and Xuanzong they all sent tribute missions to court.

sentences.zh: 水真臘國，其境東西南北約員八百里，東至奔陀浪州，西至墮羅缽底國，南至小海，北即陸真臘。

translations.literal: The state of Water Zhenla: its territory east, west, south, and north is approximately eight hundred li in circumference; east to Bentuolang Prefecture, west to the state of Duoluobodi, south to the small sea, north adjoining Land Zhenla.
translations.idiomatic: Water Chenla's territory measures roughly eight hundred li in circumference, reaching east to Bentuolang, west to Duoluobodi, south to the inner sea, and north to Land Chenla.

sentences.zh: 其王所居城號婆羅提拔。

translations.literal: The city where its king dwells is called Boluotiba.
translations.idiomatic: The king's residence is the city called Boluotiba.

sentences.zh: 國之東界有小城，皆謂之國。

translations.literal: On the eastern border of the state are small cities, all called states.
translations.idiomatic: Along its eastern frontier stand small walled settlements, each styled a kingdom in its own right.

sentences.zh: 其國多象，元和八年，遣李摩那等來朝。

translations.literal: Its state has many elephants; in the eighth year of Yuanhe, it sent Li Monuo and others to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Elephants are plentiful there; in the eighth year of Yuanhe (813) Li Monuo and others came to court.

sentences.zh: 陀洹國，在林邑西南大海中，東南與墮和羅接，去交趾三月余日行。

translations.literal: The state of Tuohuan is in the great southwestern sea from Linyi; southeast it adjoins Duohailuo; from Jiaozhi more than three months' travel.
translations.idiomatic: Tuohuan lies in the open sea southwest of Linyi, bordering Duohailuo on the southeast; from Jiaozhi it is a voyage of more than three months.

sentences.zh: 賓服於墮和羅。

translations.literal: It attends and submits to Duohailuo.
translations.idiomatic: It acknowledges the overlordship of Duohailuo.

sentences.zh: 其王姓察失利，字婆末婆那。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Chashili; his style is Bomobona.
translations.idiomatic: The king's surname is Chashili and his style Bomobona.

sentences.zh: 土無蠶桑，以白氈朝霞布為衣。

translations.literal: The land has no silkworms or mulberry; they take white felt and dawn-glow cloth for clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Silk is unknown there; clothing is made of white felt and dawn-colored cotton cloth.

sentences.zh: 俗皆樓居，謂之「幹欄」。

translations.literal: Customarily all dwell in storied houses, called "ganlan."
translations.idiomatic: The people live in raised pile dwellings known as ganlan.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十八年，遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhenguan, they sent envoys to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Zhenguan (644) they sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，又遣使獻白鸚鵡及婆律膏，仍請馬及銅鐘，詔並給之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, again they sent envoys presenting a white parrot and bolu ointment, and moreover requested horses and bronze bells; an edict granted all.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later they sent a white parrot and bolu balm, requesting horses and bronze bells as well; an edict granted everything they asked.

sentences.zh: 訶陵國，在南方海中洲上居，東與婆利、西與墮婆登、北與真臘接，南臨大海。

translations.literal: The state of Heling dwells on an islet in the southern sea; east it adjoins Poli, west Duobadeng, north Zhenla, south facing the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: Heling occupies an island in the southern seas, bordering Poli on the east, Duobadeng on the west, and Chenla on the north, with the open ocean to the south.

sentences.zh: 豎木為城，作大屋重閣，以棕櫚皮覆之。

translations.literal: They set up timbers as a wall, make great houses with multiple tiers, and cover them with palm-bark.
translations.idiomatic: Timbers form the city wall; great multi-storied halls are roofed with palm thatch.

sentences.zh: 王坐其中，悉用象牙為床。

translations.literal: The king sits within them; all use ivory for couches.
translations.idiomatic: The king sits within, and all couches are made of ivory.

sentences.zh: 食不用匙箸，以手而撮。

translations.literal: In eating they do not use spoons and chopsticks; with the hands they pinch up food.
translations.idiomatic: They eat without spoons or chopsticks, taking food directly in the hand.

sentences.zh: 亦有文字，頗識星歷。

translations.literal: They also have writing and are fairly versed in stars and calendars.
translations.idiomatic: They possess a written script and are fairly knowledgeable in astronomy and the calendar.

sentences.zh: 俗以椰樹花為酒，其樹生花，長三尺余，大如人膊，割之取汁以成酒，味甘，飲之亦醉。

translations.literal: Custom takes coconut-palm blossoms for wine; the tree produces blossoms more than three feet long, large as a man's upper arm; cutting them they draw the juice to make wine—it is sweet in taste, and drinking it one also becomes drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Palm blossom sap serves as wine: the tree bears flowers over three feet long and thick as a man's arm; the sap is tapped to ferment a sweet liquor that intoxicates like any other wine.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十四年，遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, they sent envoys to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan (640) they sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年、四年皆遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third and fourth years of Dali, all sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third and fourth years of Dali (768–769) they sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，遣使獻僧祗僮五人、鸚鵡、頻伽鳥並異種名寶。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe, they sent envoys presenting five sangzhi youths, parrots, pinjia birds, and exotic kinds of famous treasures.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanhe (815) they sent five sangzhi youths, parrots, pinjia birds, and other rare treasures.

sentences.zh: 以其使李訶內為果毅，訶內請回授其弟，詔褒而從之。

translations.literal: Their envoy Li Henei was made a guoyi officer; Henei requested that the appointment be transferred back to confer on his younger brother; an edict praised and followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoy Li Henei was appointed a guoyi officer; he asked that the commission be transferred to his younger brother, and the court praised and granted the request.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遣使進僧祗女二人、鸚鵡、玳瑁及生犀等。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, they sent envoys presenting two sangzhi maidens, parrots, tortoise shell, and live rhinoceroses, among other things.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe (818) they sent two sangzhi maidens, parrots, tortoise shell, live rhinoceroses, and the like.

sentences.zh: 墮和羅國，南與盤盤、北與迦羅舍佛、東與真臘接，西鄰大海。

translations.literal: The state of Duohailuo: south it adjoins Panpan, north Jialuoshefo, east Zhenla; west it neighbors the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: Duohailuo borders Panpan on the south, Jialuoshefo on the north, and Chenla on the east, with the ocean on the west.

sentences.zh: 去廣州五月日行。

translations.literal: From Guangzhou five months' travel.
translations.idiomatic: It lies five months' sail from Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十二年，其王遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhenguan, its king sent envoys presenting local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhenguan (638) its king sent envoys with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，又遣使獻象牙、火珠，請賜好馬，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, again they sent envoys presenting ivory and a fire pearl, requesting bestowal of fine horses; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Zhenguan (649) they sent ivory and a fire pearl and requested fine horses; the court granted them.

sentences.zh: 墮婆登國，在林邑南，海行二月，東與訶陵、西與迷黎車接，北界大海。

translations.literal: The state of Duobadeng is south of Linyi; by sea two months; east it adjoins Heling, west Miliche; north bounded by the great sea.
translations.idiomatic: Duobadeng lies south of Linyi, two months' voyage by sea; it borders Heling on the east and Miliche on the west, with the ocean to the north.

sentences.zh: 風俗與訶陵略同。

translations.literal: Customs are roughly the same as Heling.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs closely resemble those of Heling.

sentences.zh: 其國種稻，每月一熟。

translations.literal: Its state plants rice; each month once ripens.
translations.idiomatic: Rice is cultivated there and ripens once every month.

sentences.zh: 亦有文字，書之於貝多葉。

translations.literal: They also have writing, written on pattra leaves.
translations.idiomatic: They have a script inscribed on palm-leaf manuscripts.

sentences.zh: 其死者，口實以金，又以金釧貫於四肢，然後加以婆律膏及龍腦等香，積柴以燔之。

translations.literal: For their dead, the mouth is filled with gold, and moreover gold bracelets are threaded through the four limbs; then bolu ointment and borneol and other aromatics are applied, firewood is piled, and they are burned.
translations.idiomatic: The dead receive gold in the mouth and gold bracelets on the limbs; bolu balm, borneol, and other perfumes are applied before the body is heaped with firewood and cremated.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十一年，其王遣使獻古貝、象牙、白檀，太宗璽書報之，並賜以雜物。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan, its king sent envoys presenting kapok cloth, ivory, and white sandalwood; Taizong replied with a sealed letter and also bestowed various goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan (647) its king sent kapok cloth, ivory, and white sandalwood; Taizong answered with an imperial letter and gifts of sundry goods.

sentences.zh: 東謝蠻，其地在黔州之西數百里，南接守宮獠，西連夷子，北至蠻。

translations.literal: The Eastern Xie Man: their land is several hundred li west of Qian Prefecture; south it adjoins the Shougong Liao, west it connects with the Yizi, north reaching to the Man.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Xie tribes dwell several hundred li west of Qian Prefecture, adjoining the Shougong Liao on the south, the Yizi on the west, and other Man peoples on the north.

sentences.zh: 土宜五谷，不以牛耕，但為畬田，每歲易。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains; they do not plow with oxen but only make slash-and-burn fields, changing them each year.
translations.idiomatic: The soil supports the five grains; they do not plow with oxen but cultivate slash-and-burn fields, shifting plots every year.

sentences.zh: 俗無文字，刻木為契。

translations.literal: Custom has no writing; they carve wood to make contracts.
translations.idiomatic: They have no written script and record agreements by carving notches in wood.

sentences.zh: 散在山洞間，依樹為層巢而居，汲流以飲。

translations.literal: Scattered among mountain caves, they rely on trees to make layered nests for dwelling and draw stream water to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered among mountain caves, they build tiered tree-house nests and draw water from streams to drink.

sentences.zh: 皆自營生業，無賦稅之事。

translations.literal: All manage their own livelihoods; there are no matters of levies and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Each household provides for itself; there are no taxes or levies.

sentences.zh: 謁見貴人，皆執鞭而拜；

translations.literal: When paying respects to eminent persons, all hold whips and bow;
translations.idiomatic: When meeting persons of rank they all bow while holding whips;

sentences.zh: 有功勞者，以牛馬銅鼓賞之。

translations.literal: those with merit and achievement are rewarded with cattle, horses, and bronze drums.
translations.idiomatic: those who distinguish themselves are rewarded with cattle, horses, and bronze drums.

sentences.zh: 有犯罪者，小事杖罰之，大事殺之，盜物倍還其贓。

translations.literal: Those who commit crimes: minor matters are punished with the staff; major matters are killed; stolen goods are returned double the booty.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders receive beating for minor crimes and execution for major ones; thieves must restore double the value of what they stole.

sentences.zh: 婚姻之禮，以牛酒為聘。

translations.literal: The rites of marriage take cattle and wine as betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage gifts consist of cattle and wine.

sentences.zh: 女婦夫家，皆母自送之。

translations.literal: When a woman weds into her husband's house, the mother always escorts her herself.
translations.idiomatic: When a daughter marries, her mother always escorts her to the groom's home.

sentences.zh: 女夫慚，逃避經旬乃出。

translations.literal: The son-in-law is ashamed and flees, hiding for more than ten days before emerging.
translations.idiomatic: The new husband, overcome with embarrassment, hides away for ten days or more before appearing.

sentences.zh: 宴聚則擊銅鼓，吹大角，歌舞以為樂。

translations.literal: At feasts and gatherings they strike bronze drums, blow great horns, and sing and dance for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: At gatherings they beat bronze drums, blow great horns, and sing and dance for entertainment.

sentences.zh: 好帶刀劍，未嘗舍離。

translations.literal: They delight in wearing swords and blades and never set them aside.
translations.idiomatic: They are fond of carrying swords and never go without them.

sentences.zh: 丈夫衣服，有衫襖大口褲，以綿綢及布為之。

translations.literal: Men's clothing includes jackets, padded coats, and baggy trousers, made of cotton silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Men wear jackets, padded coats, and loose trousers of cotton, silk, or plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 右肩上斜束皮帶，裝以螺殼、虎豹猿狖及犬羊之皮，以為外飾。

translations.literal: On the right shoulder a leather belt is bound diagonally, adorned with shells, tiger, leopard, ape, and dog and sheep skins as outer ornament.
translations.idiomatic: A leather belt is slung diagonally from the right shoulder, decorated with shells and the pelts of tigers, leopards, apes, dogs, and sheep as outer adornment.

sentences.zh: 坐皆蹲踞。

translations.literal: In sitting, all squat on their heels.
translations.idiomatic: They always sit squatting on their heels.

sentences.zh: 男女椎髻，以緋束之，後垂向下。

translations.literal: Men and women wear topknots, bound with scarlet cloth, hanging down behind.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women wear topknots bound with scarlet cloth, the hair hanging down the back.

sentences.zh: 其首領謝元深，既世為酋長，其部落皆尊畏之。

translations.literal: Their chieftain Xie Yuanshen, having been chieftain for generations, is revered and feared by all his tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain Xie Yuanshen, head of a hereditary line, is revered and feared by all his tribes.

sentences.zh: 謝氏一族，法不育女，自雲高姓不可下嫁故也。

translations.literal: The Xie clan by law does not rear daughters, saying themselves that a lofty surname may not marry downward.
translations.idiomatic: By clan law the Xie do not raise daughters, holding that their exalted surname must not marry beneath itself.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，元深入朝，冠烏熊皮冠，若今之髦頭，以金銀絡額，身披毛帔，韋皮行滕而著履，中書侍郎顏師古奏言：「昔周武王時，天下太平，遠國歸款，周史乃書其事為《王會篇》。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, Yuanshen came to court, wearing a black bear-skin cap like today's maotou, with gold and silver netting the forehead, a fur cape on the body, leather leggings and shoes; Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu memorialized saying: "Of old in King Wu of Zhou's time, the realm was at peace, distant states came in allegiance, and the Zhou historians wrote the matter as the Royal Assembly Record.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan (629) Yuanshen came to court wearing a black bear-skin cap like the maotou of the day, gold and silver netting his brow, a fur cape on his shoulders, and leather leggings and shoes. Vice Director of the Secretariat Yan Shigu memorialized: "In the time of King Wu of Zhou, when the realm was at peace and distant states came to pay homage, the Zhou historians recorded the event in the Royal Assembly Record.

sentences.zh: 今萬國來朝，至於此輩章服，實可圖寫，今請撰為《王會圖》。

translations.literal: Now the ten thousand states come to court; as for the dress and regalia of these people, they truly can be drawn and painted; I now request that they be compiled as Illustrations of the Royal Assembly."
translations.idiomatic: Now the myriad states attend court, and the dress of these envoys can truly be painted. I request that an Illustrations of the Royal Assembly be compiled."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 以其地為應州，仍拜元深為刺史，領黔州都督府。

translations.literal: Taking their land as Ying Prefecture, Yuanshen was moreover appointed prefect and placed in charge of the Qianzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Their territory was organized as Ying Prefecture, and Yuanshen was appointed prefect under the Qianzhou area command.

sentences.zh: 又有南謝首領謝強，與西謝鄰，共元深俱來朝見，為南壽州刺史。

translations.literal: There was also the Southern Xie chieftain Xie Qiang, neighboring the Western Xie, who together with Yuanshen came to court and was made prefect of Nanshou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Xie chieftain Xie Qiang, whose territory bordered the Western Xie, came to court with Yuanshen and was appointed prefect of Nanshou.

sentences.zh: 後改為莊州。

translations.literal: Later it was changed to Zhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was later renamed Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 貞元十三年正月，西南蕃大酋長、正議大夫、檢校蠻州長史，繼襲蠻州刺史，資陽郡開國公、賜紫金魚袋宋鼎，左右大首領、朝散大夫、前檢校邛州刺史、賜紫金魚袋謝汕，左右大首領、繼襲攝蠻州巴江縣令、賜紫金魚袋宋萬傳，界首子弟大首領、朝散大夫、牂州錄事參軍謝文經。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan, the great chieftain of the southwestern tribes Song Ding—Grand Master of Palace Counsel, acting military commissioner of Man Prefecture, succeeding as prefect of Man Prefecture, Duke of Ziyang commandery with a fief state, granted the purple-gold fish tally—and the great chiefs of left and right Xie Shan and Song Wanchuan, and the great chief of the border Xie Wenjing, came.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan (797), the great southwestern chieftains Song Ding, Xie Shan, Song Wanchuan, and Xie Wenjing—bearing ranks from Grand Master of Palace Counsel down to military registrar of Zang Prefecture, with purple-gold fish tallies and hereditary offices—presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 黔中經略招討觀察使王礎奏：「前件刺史，建中三年一度朝貢，自後更不許隨例入朝。

translations.literal: The Qianzhong frontier commissioner Wang Ji memorialized: "The aforesaid prefects in the third year of Jianzhong once came to court with tribute; from then on they were no longer permitted to enter court according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, frontier commissioner of Qianzhong, memorialized: "These prefects paid court tribute once in the third year of Jianzhong (782) but have since been barred from the customary audience.

sentences.zh: 今年懇訴稱州接牂牁，同被聲教，獨此排擯，竊自慚恥，謹遣隨牂牁等朝賀。

translations.literal: This year they earnestly petitioned, saying their prefecture adjoins Zangge, equally receiving the transforming voice, yet this alone is excluded and rejected; they secretly feel shame, and respectfully send envoys to follow Zangge and others in court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: This year they pleaded that their prefecture, like Zangge, lies within the transforming influence of the court yet alone has been excluded—a source of shame—and have sent envoys to join Zangge in the New Year audience.

sentences.zh: 伏乞特賜優諭，兼同牂牁刺史授官。

translations.literal: They humbly beg special gracious instruction, and moreover the same conferral of office as the Zangge prefect.
translations.idiomatic: They beg a special gracious edict and appointment to office equal to that of the Zangge prefect.

sentences.zh: 其牂牁兩州，戶口殷盛，人力強大，鄰側諸蕃，悉皆敬憚。

translations.literal: These two prefectures of Zangge have flourishing households and population, strong manpower; the neighboring tribes all revere and fear them.
translations.idiomatic: The two Zangge prefectures are populous and strong, and the neighboring tribes all hold them in awe.

sentences.zh: 請比兩州每年一度朝貢，仍依牂牁輪環差定，並以才幹位望為眾推者充。

translations.literal: I request that they be compared to the two prefectures in coming once a year with tribute, still following Zangge's rotation in turn, and that those whom the multitude recommends for talent, ability, standing, and reputation fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be allowed an annual tribute audience on the same rotation as the two Zangge prefectures, with offices filled by men of talent and standing whom the tribes recommend.

sentences.zh: 」敕旨曰：「宋鼎等已改官訖，余依舊。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Song Ding and the others have already had their offices changed; the rest follows the old practice."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Song Ding and the others have received new appointments; the remainder follows established practice."

sentences.zh: 西趙蠻，在東謝之南，其界東至夷子，西至昆明，南至西洱河。

translations.literal: The Western Zhao Man are south of the Eastern Xie; their border east reaches the Yizi, west reaches Kunming, south reaches the Western Er River.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Zhao tribes lie south of the Eastern Xie, reaching east to the Yizi, west to Kunming, and south to the Western Er River.

sentences.zh: 山洞阻深，莫知道里。

translations.literal: Mountain caves are obstructed and deep; none knows the roads and distances.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain caves and ravines make the routes impenetrable and distances unknown.

sentences.zh: 南北十八日行，東西二十三日行。

translations.literal: North and south eighteen days' travel; east and west twenty-three days' travel.
translations.idiomatic: The territory measures eighteen days' journey north to south and twenty-three days east to west.

sentences.zh: 其風俗物產與東謝同。

translations.literal: Their customs and products are the same as the Eastern Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and products match those of the Eastern Xie.

sentences.zh: 首領趙氏。

translations.literal: The chieftains are of the Zhao clan.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains belong to the Zhao clan.

sentences.zh: 世為酋長。

translations.literal: For generations they have been chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftaincy passes through the Zhao line for generations.

sentences.zh: 有戶萬余。

translations.literal: There are more than ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The population exceeds ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，遣使入朝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan, they sent envoys to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan (629) they sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以其地置明州，以首領趙磨為刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, taking their land they established Ming Prefecture and made the chieftain Zhao Mo prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Zhenguan (647) their territory was organized as Ming Prefecture under the chieftain Zhao Mo.

sentences.zh: 牂牁蠻，首領亦姓謝氏。

translations.literal: The Zangge Man: the chieftains also bear the surname Xie.
translations.idiomatic: The Zangge tribes are also led by the Xie clan.

sentences.zh: 其地北去兗州一百五十里，東至辰州二千四百里，南至交州一千五百里，西至昆明九百里。

translations.literal: Its land is one hundred fifty li north of Yan Prefecture, two thousand four hundred li east to Chen Prefecture, one thousand five hundred li south to Jiaozhou, nine hundred li west to Kunming.
translations.idiomatic: From Yan Prefecture it lies one hundred fifty li to the north, Chen Prefecture two thousand four hundred li to the east, Jiaozhou one thousand five hundred li to the south, and Kunming nine hundred li to the west.

sentences.zh: 無城壁，散為部落而居。

translations.literal: There are no walls; they are scattered as tribes dwelling apart.
translations.idiomatic: There are no walled cities; the people live scattered in tribal settlements.

sentences.zh: 土氣郁熱，多霖雨。

translations.literal: The climate of the soil is sultry and hot; there is much rainy season rain.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is humid and torrid, with frequent rains.

sentences.zh: 稻粟再熟。

translations.literal: Rice and millet ripen twice.
translations.idiomatic: Rice and millet are harvested twice a year.

sentences.zh: 無徭役，唯征戰之時，乃相屯聚。

translations.literal: There is no corvée labor; only when campaigning for war do they gather and mass together.
translations.idiomatic: There is no corvée labor; the tribes assemble only when war is at hand.

sentences.zh: 刻木為契。

translations.literal: They carve wood for contracts.
translations.idiomatic: Agreements are recorded by carving wood.

sentences.zh: 其法：劫盜者二倍還贓；

translations.literal: Their law: robbers and plunderers return double the booty;
translations.idiomatic: By their law, robbers must restore double the stolen goods;

sentences.zh: 殺人者出牛馬三十頭，乃得贖死，以納死家。

translations.literal: killers produce thirty head of cattle and horses and then may ransom death, presenting them to the family of the dead.
translations.idiomatic: murderers may ransom their lives with thirty head of cattle and horses paid to the victim's family.

sentences.zh: 風俗物產，略與東謝同。

translations.literal: Customs and products are roughly the same as the Eastern Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and products broadly resemble those of the Eastern Xie.

sentences.zh: 其首領謝龍羽，大業末據其地，勝兵數萬人。

translations.literal: Its chieftain Xie Longyu at the end of Daye seized its land, with several tens of thousands of effective troops.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain Xie Longyu seized the territory at the end of the Sui and commanded tens of thousands of fighting men.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，遣使朝貢，授龍羽牂州刺史，封夜郎郡公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, they sent envoys to court with tribute; Longyu was appointed prefect of Zang Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Yelang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wude (620) they sent tribute envoys; Longyu was appointed prefect of Zang and enfeoffed Duke of Yelang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年十二月，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Zhenguan, they sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Zhenguan (630) they sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 開元十年閏五月，大酋長謝元齊死，詔立其嫡孫嘉藝襲其官封。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year of Kaiyuan, the great chieftain Xie Yuanqi died; an edict installed his eldest grandson Jiayi to succeed to his office and fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of the tenth year of Kaiyuan (722) the great chieftain Xie Yuanqi died; an edict installed his eldest grandson Jiayi in his offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，大酋長趙君道來朝，且獻方物，大歷中、貞元初，數遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the great chieftain Zhao Jundao came to court and moreover presented local products; in the Dali era and early Zhenyuan, they repeatedly sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan (737) the great chieftain Zhao Jundao came to court with local products; during the Dali and early Zhenyuan eras they sent frequent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，授其酋長趙主俗官，以其歲初朝貢不絕，褒之也。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, their chieftain Zhao Zhu was granted an official post, because from the year's beginning tribute missions did not cease—this was to commend them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year of Zhenyuan (791) their chieftain Zhao Zhu was granted an official post in recognition of his unbroken New Year tribute.

sentences.zh: 自七年至十八年，凡五遣使來。

translations.literal: From the seventh year to the eighteenth, in all five times they sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Between the seventh and eighteenth years they sent envoys five times.

sentences.zh: 元和三年五月敕：「自今以後，委黔南觀察使差本道軍將充押領牂牁、昆明等使。

translations.literal: An edict of the fifth month of the third year of Yuanhe: "From now onward, charge the Qiannan observation commissioner to dispatch military officers of this circuit to serve as escorts leading the Zangge, Kunming, and other missions."
translations.idiomatic: An edict of the fifth month of the third year of Yuanhe (808) directed: "Henceforth the Qiannan observation commissioner shall assign military officers of the circuit to escort Zangge, Kunming, and other missions."

sentences.zh: 」四年正月，遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, they sent envoys to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Yuanhe (809) they sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 是月，遣中使魏德和領其使，並賫國信物，降璽書賜其王焉。

translations.literal: That month, a palace envoy Wei Dehe was dispatched to lead their mission, bearing also state credence objects; an imperial sealed letter was sent down bestowing on their king.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the palace envoy Wei Dehe was sent to escort their mission with state gifts and an imperial letter for their king.

sentences.zh: 七年、九年、十一年，凡三遣使來。

translations.literal: In the seventh, ninth, and eleventh years, in all three times they sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh, ninth, and eleventh years they sent missions three times.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，又遣使來賀正。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, again they sent envoys to come and congratulate the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year they again sent envoys for the New Year audience.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，亦朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: In the Changqing era, tribute missions to court also did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing era their tribute missions likewise continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年十二月，遣使謝良震來朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Baoli, they sent the envoy Xie Liangzhen to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first year of Baoli (825) they sent the envoy Xie Liangzhen to court.

sentences.zh: 太和五年至會昌二年，凡七遣使來。

translations.literal: From the fifth year of Taihe to the second year of Huichang, in all seven times they sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: From the fifth year of Taihe (831) to the second year of Huichang (842) they sent envoys seven times.

sentences.zh: 南平獠者，東與智州、南與渝州、西與南州、北與涪州接。

translations.literal: The Nanping Liao: east they adjoin Zhi Prefecture, south Yuzhou, west Nan Prefecture, north Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanping Liao border Zhi Prefecture on the east, Yuzhou on the south, Nan Prefecture on the west, and Fu Prefecture on the north.

sentences.zh: 部落四千余戶。

translations.literal: The tribes number more than four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: They comprise more than four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 土氣多瘴癘，山有毒草及沙虱、蝮蛇。

translations.literal: The climate of the soil has much miasmal pestilence; in the mountains are poisonous plants and sand fleas and pit vipers.
translations.idiomatic: Malarial miasma is rife, and the mountains harbor poisonous plants, sand fleas, and pit vipers.

sentences.zh: 人並樓居，登梯而上。

translations.literal: The people all dwell in storied houses, climbing ladders to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: All live in raised dwellings reached by ladder.

sentences.zh: 號為「幹欄」。

translations.literal: They are called "ganlan."
translations.idiomatic: These are called ganlan.

sentences.zh: 男子左衽露發徒跣；

translations.literal: Men wear the left lapel, bare the hair, and go barefoot;
translations.idiomatic: Men wear the left lapel, leave their hair loose, and go barefoot;

sentences.zh: 婦人橫布兩幅，穿中而貫其首，名為「通裙」。

translations.literal: women take two horizontal cloth panels, pierce the middle and thread the head through, called a "tong skirt."
translations.idiomatic: women wear a garment of two horizontal cloth panels with the head passed through the middle, called a tong skirt.

sentences.zh: 其人美發，為髻鬟垂於後。

translations.literal: Their people have beautiful hair, made into coiled buns hanging behind.
translations.idiomatic: They have fine hair worn in coiled buns down the back.

sentences.zh: 以竹筒如筆，長三四寸，斜貫其耳，貴者亦有珠榼。

translations.literal: They take bamboo tubes like pens, three or four inches long, run diagonally through the ear; the eminent also have pearl plugs.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo tubes three or four inches long, like writing brushes, are worn diagonally through the ears; the wealthy also wear pearl plugs.

sentences.zh: 土多女少男，為婚之法，女氏必先貨求男族，貧者無以嫁女，多賣與富人為婢。

translations.literal: The land has many women and few men; in the law of marriage the woman's clan must first pay goods to seek the man's clan; the poor have no means to marry daughters off and mostly sell them to the rich as maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: Women outnumber men; by marriage custom the bride's clan must first pay the groom's clan, and the poor, unable to marry off their daughters, often sell them as maidservants to the wealthy.

sentences.zh: 俗皆婦人執役。

translations.literal: Customarily all labor is performed by women.
translations.idiomatic: By custom women perform all the labor.

sentences.zh: 其王姓硃氏，號為劍荔王，遣使內附，以其地隸於渝州。

translations.literal: Their king's surname is Zhu; he is styled King Jianli; he sent envoys to submit internally, and his land was placed under Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Their king, surnamed Zhu and styled King Jianli, sent envoys to submit; his territory was placed under Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 東女國，西羌之別種，以西海中復有女國，故稱東女焉。

translations.literal: The Eastern Women's State is a separate branch of the Western Qiang; because in the Western Sea there is again a Women's State, it is therefore called Eastern Women.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Women's State is a branch of the Western Qiang; because another Women's State lies beyond the western sea, this one is called the Eastern Women's State.

sentences.zh: 俗以女為王。

translations.literal: Custom takes a woman as king.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a woman holds the throne.

sentences.zh: 東與茂州、党項接，東南與雅州接，界隔羅女蠻及白狼夷。

translations.literal: East it adjoins Mao Prefecture and the Tangut; southeast it adjoins Ya Prefecture; the border separates it from the Luonü Man and the White Wolf Yi.
translations.idiomatic: It borders Mao Prefecture and the Tangut on the east and Ya Prefecture on the southeast, with the Luonü Man and White Wolf Yi in between.

sentences.zh: 其境東西九日行，南北二十日行。

translations.literal: Its territory is nine days' travel east and west, twenty days north and south.
translations.idiomatic: The realm measures nine days' journey east to west and twenty days north to south.

sentences.zh: 有大小八十余城。

translations.literal: There are more than eighty great and small cities.
translations.idiomatic: It contains more than eighty cities large and small.

sentences.zh: 其王所居名康延川，中有弱水南流，用牛皮為船以渡。

translations.literal: Where the king dwells is called Kangyanchuan; within it the Weak Water flows south; they use oxhide for boats to cross.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is Kangyanchuan, through which the Weak Water flows southward; crossings are made in boats of oxhide.

sentences.zh: 戶四萬余眾，勝兵萬余人，散在山谷間。

translations.literal: Households number more than forty thousand souls; effective troops more than ten thousand, scattered among valleys and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: The population exceeds forty thousand households with more than ten thousand fighting men scattered through the valleys.

sentences.zh: 女王號為「賓就」。

translations.literal: The queen is styled "Binjiu."
translations.idiomatic: The queen bears the title Binjiu.

sentences.zh: 有女官，曰「高霸」，平議國事。

translations.literal: There are female officials called "Gaoba" who discuss and settle state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Female officials called Gaoba deliberate on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 在外官僚，並男夫為之。

translations.literal: The officials outside are all performed by men.
translations.idiomatic: External offices are all held by men.

sentences.zh: 其王侍女數百人，五日一聽政。

translations.literal: The king's attendant women number several hundred; every five days she once hears government.
translations.idiomatic: The queen is attended by several hundred women and holds audience every five days.

sentences.zh: 女王若死，國中多斂金錢，動至數萬，更於王族求令女二人而立之。

translations.literal: If the queen dies, within the state much gold and money is collected, often reaching tens of thousands; again from the royal clan they seek two worthy daughters and install them.
translations.idiomatic: When a queen dies, the state collects gold and coin by the tens of thousands and selects two worthy daughters of the royal clan to succeed her.

sentences.zh: 大者為王，其次為小王。

translations.literal: The elder becomes king, the second becomes lesser king.
translations.idiomatic: The elder becomes the Great Queen, the younger the Lesser Queen.

sentences.zh: 若大王死，即小王嗣立，或姑死而婦繼，無有篡奪。

translations.literal: If the great queen dies, the lesser queen succeeds and is installed; sometimes an aunt dies and a daughter-in-law succeeds—there is no usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: If the Great Queen dies, the Lesser Queen succeeds; sometimes an aunt's daughter-in-law inherits—usurpation is unknown.

sentences.zh: 其所居，皆起重屋，王至九層，國人至六層。

translations.literal: Where they dwell, all erect lofty houses; the king up to nine tiers, the people of the state up to six tiers.
translations.idiomatic: Dwellings are built as towered houses—the queen's up to nine stories, those of her subjects up to six.

sentences.zh: 其王服青毛綾裙，下領衫，上披青袍，其袖委地。

translations.literal: The queen wears a green woolen damask skirt, a collared shirt below, and a green robe above; the sleeves trail on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The queen wears a green wool damask skirt and collared undershirt beneath a green robe with sleeves trailing to the ground.

sentences.zh: 冬則羔裘，飾以紋錦。

translations.literal: In winter she wears lamb fur, adorned with patterned brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In winter she wears lamb fur trimmed with brocade.

sentences.zh: 為小鬟髻，飾之以金。

translations.literal: She makes small coiled buns, adorning them with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Her hair is worn in small coiled buns adorned with gold.

sentences.zh: 耳垂榼，足履索蜺。

translations.literal: Her ears hang with plugs; her feet wear sandals.
translations.idiomatic: She wears ear plugs and sandals on her feet.

sentences.zh: 俗重婦人而輕丈夫。

translations.literal: Custom esteems women and treats husbands lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Women are held in honor and men in low regard.

sentences.zh: 文字同於天竺。

translations.literal: Writing is the same as India.
translations.idiomatic: Their script is the same as that of India.

sentences.zh: 以十一月為正。

translations.literal: They take the eleventh month as the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh month is reckoned the start of the year.

sentences.zh: 其俗每至十月，令巫者賫楮詣山中，散糟麥於空，大咒呼鳥。

translations.literal: Their custom every year when the tenth month arrives orders shamans to carry paper to the mountains, scatter lees and grain in the open, and loudly incant to call birds.
translations.idiomatic: Each tenth month shamans carry paper offerings into the mountains, scatter grain and lees in the open air, and chant loudly to summon birds.

sentences.zh: 俄而有鳥如雞，飛入巫者之懷，因剖腹而視之，每有一谷，來歲必登，若有霜雪，必多災異。

translations.literal: Shortly a bird like a chicken flies into the shaman's bosom; then they cut open the belly and look within—each grain means the coming year will surely have a good harvest; if there is frost and snow, there will surely be many disasters and anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Presently a chicken-sized bird flies into the shaman's arms; its belly is opened and inspected—each grain found foretells a good harvest the following year, while frost or snow portends many calamities.

sentences.zh: 其俗信之，名為鳥卜。

translations.literal: Their custom believes in it; it is called bird divination.
translations.idiomatic: They trust this practice, which they call bird divination.

sentences.zh: 其居喪，服飾不改，為父母則三年不櫛沐。

translations.literal: In dwelling in mourning, dress and adornment are not changed; for parents they do not comb the hair or bathe for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning they do not change their dress; for parents they neither comb their hair nor bathe for three years.

sentences.zh: 貴人死者，或剝其皮而藏之，內骨於瓶中，糅以金屑而埋之。

translations.literal: When eminent persons die, sometimes they flay the skin and store it, place the bones in a jar, mix with gold filings, and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: When nobles die, sometimes the skin is flayed and preserved, the bones placed in a jar mixed with gold dust, and buried.

sentences.zh: 國王將葬，其大臣親屬殉死者數十人。

translations.literal: When the queen is about to be buried, her great ministers and kin who follow in death number several tens.
translations.idiomatic: When a queen is buried, dozens of her ministers and relatives follow her in death.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，蜀王秀遣使招之，拒而不受。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, Prince Xiu of Shu sent envoys to summon them; they refused and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era of Sui, Prince Xiu of Shu sent envoys to summon them, but they refused.

sentences.zh: 武德中，女王湯滂氏始遣使貢方物，高祖厚資而遣之。

translations.literal: In Wude, Queen Tangbangshi first sent envoys presenting local products; Gaozu richly rewarded them and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude, Queen Tangbangshi first sent tribute envoys; Gaozu rewarded them generously and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 還至隴右，會突厥入寇，被掠於虜庭。

translations.literal: Returning to Longyou, they encountered Turkic invasion and were seized in the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: On the return through Longyou they met a Turkic raid and were carried off to the steppe.

sentences.zh: 及頡利平，其使復來入朝。

translations.literal: When Jieli was pacified, their envoys again came to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli was subdued, their envoys came to court again.

sentences.zh: 太宗送令反國，並降璽書慰撫之。

translations.literal: Taizong sent them back ordering return to their state and also sent down an imperial sealed letter to comfort and soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent them home with an imperial letter of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 垂拱二年，其王斂臂遣大臣湯劍左來朝，仍請官號。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong, its queen Lianbi sent the great minister Tang Jianzuo to come to court and moreover requested an official title.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chuigong (686) Queen Lianbi sent the minister Tang Jianzuo to court to request an official title.

sentences.zh: 則天冊拜斂臂為左玉鈐衛員外將軍，仍以瑞錦制蕃服以賜之。

translations.literal: Zetian enfeoffed Lianbi as acting general of the Left Jade Bell Guard and moreover made barbarian dress from auspicious brocade to bestow on her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu appointed Lianbi acting general of the Left Jade Bell Guard and granted her barbarian dress of auspicious brocade.

sentences.zh: 貞元九年七月，其王湯立悉與哥鄰國王董臥庭、白狗國王羅陀忽、逋租國王弟鄧吉知、南水國王侄薛尚悉曩、弱水國王董辟和、悉董國王湯息贊、清遠國王蘇唐磨、咄霸國王董藐蓬，各率其種落詣劍南西川內附。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan, its king Tang Lixi together with the king of Geling Dong Woting, the king of Baigou Luotuohu, the younger brother of the king of Bozu Deng Jizhi, the nephew of the king of Nanshui Xue Shangxinang, the king of Ruoshui Dong Pihe, the king of Xidong Tang Xizan, the king of Qingyuan Su Tangmo, and the king of Duoba Dong Miaopeng, each leading their tribes and clans, came to Jiannan West River to submit internally.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan (793) Queen Tang Lixi, together with the kings of Geling, Baigou, Bozu, Nanshui, Ruoshui, Xidong, Qingyuan, and Duoba and their tribes, came to Jiannan West River to submit.

sentences.zh: 其哥鄰國等，皆散居山川。

translations.literal: These states such as Geling all dwell scattered among mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Geling and the other states all live scattered among mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 弱水王即國初女國之弱水部落。

translations.literal: The king of Ruoshui is the Ruoshui tribe of the Women's State at the beginning of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The Ruoshui king belongs to the Ruoshui tribe of the early Women's State.

sentences.zh: 其悉董國，在弱水西，故亦謂之弱水西悉董王。

translations.literal: Its Xidong state is west of Ruoshui; therefore it is also called the Xidong king west of Ruoshui.
translations.idiomatic: Xidong lies west of Ruoshui and is also known as the Xidong king west of the Weak Water.

sentences.zh: 舊皆分隸邊郡，祖、父例授將軍、中郎、果毅等官，自中原多故，皆為吐蕃所役屬。

translations.literal: Formerly all were separately attached to frontier prefectures; grandfathers and fathers by precedent were appointed generals, palace gentlemen, guoyi officers, and the like; since the central plains had many troubles, all were made subject and subordinate to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: They had long been attached to frontier prefectures, their forebears appointed generals, palace gentlemen, and guoyi officers; since turmoil in the central plains they had all fallen under Tibetan control.

sentences.zh: 其部落，大者不過三二千戶，各置縣令十數人理之。

translations.literal: Their tribes, the largest not exceeding two or three thousand households, each had more than ten county magistrates to administer them.
translations.idiomatic: The largest tribes numbered no more than two or three thousand households, each administered by a dozen or so magistrates.

sentences.zh: 土有絲絮，歲輸於吐蕃。

translations.literal: The land produces silk floss; each year it was delivered to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The land produces silk floss, which they paid annually to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 至是悉與之同盟，相率獻款，兼賫天寶中國家所賜官誥共三十九通以進。

translations.literal: At this time all formed alliance with them, leading one another in presenting allegiance, and moreover brought the thirty-nine patents of office bestowed by the state in the Tianbao era to present.
translations.idiomatic: Now they all joined in alliance, came forward in allegiance together, and presented the thirty-nine patents of office granted in the Tianbao era.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使韋臯處其眾於維、霸、保等州，給以種糧耕牛，鹹樂生業。

translations.literal: The Jiannan West River frontier commissioner Wei Gao settled their multitudes in Wei, Ba, Bao, and other prefectures, supplied them with seed grain and plow oxen, and all rejoiced in their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao, commissioner of Jiannan West River, settled them in Wei, Ba, Bao, and other prefectures, providing seed grain and oxen until they were content in their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 立悉等數國王自來朝，召見於麟德殿。

translations.literal: Lixi and several kings came to court in person and were summoned to audience in the Linde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Lixi and several kings came to court in person and were received in the Linde Hall.

sentences.zh: 授立悉銀青光祿大夫、歸化州刺史；

translations.literal: Lixi was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and prefect of Guihua Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Lixi was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and prefect of Guihua;

sentences.zh: 鄧吉知試太府少卿兼丹州長史；

translations.literal: Deng Jizhi was made acting vice minister of the Grand Storehouse and concurrently chief administrator of Dan Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jizhi was made acting vice minister of the Grand Storehouse and chief administrator of Dan Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 薛尚悉曩試少府少監兼霸州長史；

translations.literal: Xue Shangxinang was made acting vice director of the Palace Storehouse and concurrently chief administrator of Ba Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shangxinang was made acting vice director of the Palace Storehouse and chief administrator of Ba Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 董臥庭行至綿州卒，贈武德州刺史，命其子利啰為保守都督府長史，襲哥鄰王。

translations.literal: Dong Woting died on reaching Mian Prefecture; he was posthumously granted prefect of Wude Prefecture, and his son Lila was ordered as chief administrator of the Baoshou area command to succeed as king of Geling.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Woting died at Mian Prefecture and was posthumously made prefect of Wude; his son Lila was appointed chief administrator of Baoshou and succeeded as king of Geling.

sentences.zh: 立悉妹乞悉漫頗有才智，從其兄來朝，封和義郡夫人。

translations.literal: Lixi's younger sister Qiximan was quite talented and intelligent; following her elder brother to court, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Heyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lixi's sister Qiximan, a woman of considerable talent, accompanied her brother to court and was enfeoffed Lady of Heyi.

sentences.zh: 其大首領董臥卿等，皆授以官。

translations.literal: Their great chieftains Dong Woqing and the others were all granted offices.
translations.idiomatic: Their great chieftains, including Dong Woqing, were all granted offices.

sentences.zh: 俄又授女國王兄湯厥銀青光祿大夫、試太府卿；

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the elder brother of the Women's State queen Tang Jue was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master and acting minister of the Grand Storehouse;
translations.idiomatic: Soon the queen's brother Tang Jue was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master and acting minister of the Grand Storehouse;

sentences.zh: 清遠王弟蘇歷顛銀青光祿大夫、試衛尉卿；

translations.literal: the younger brother of the Qingyuan king Su Lidian was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master and acting minister of the Imperial Guard;
translations.idiomatic: the Qingyuan king's brother Su Lidian was appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master and acting minister of the Imperial Guard;

sentences.zh: 南水國王薛莫庭及湯息贊、董藐蓬，女國唱後湯拂庭、美玉缽、南郎唐，並授銀青光祿大夫、試太仆卿。

translations.literal: the king of Nanshui Xue Moting, Tang Xizan, Dong Miaopeng, the Women's State queen's consort Tang Futing, Meiyubo, and Nanlang Tang were all appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master and acting minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: the Nanshui king Xue Moting, Tang Xizan, Dong Miaopeng, the queen's consort Tang Futing, Meiyubo, and Nanlang Tang were all appointed Silver-Gleam Grand Master and acting minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 其年，西山松州生羌等二萬余戶，相繼內附。

translations.literal: That year, more than twenty thousand households of the raw Qiang of Song Prefecture in the western hills successively submitted internally.
translations.idiomatic: That year more than twenty thousand households of the western Song Prefecture Qiang submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 其粘信部落主董夢蔥，龍諾部落主董辟忽，皆授試衛尉卿。

translations.literal: The chieftain of the Zhanxin tribe Dong Mengcong and the chieftain of the Longnuo tribe Dong Pihu were both appointed acting minister of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhanxin chieftain Dong Mengcong and the Longnuo chieftain Dong Pihu were both appointed acting minister of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 立悉等並赴明年元會訖，錫以金帛，各遣還。

translations.literal: Lixi and the others all attended the next year's New Year assembly; they were granted gold and silks and each sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Lixi and the others attended the New Year assembly, received gifts of gold and silk, and were sent home.

sentences.zh: 尋詔加韋臯統押近界羌、蠻及西山八國使。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict added to Wei Gao overall command as escort commissioner for the near-border Qiang, Man, and the eight states of the western hills.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon added to Wei Gao's duties overall command of the near-border Qiang, Man, and the eight western hill states.

sentences.zh: 其部落代襲刺史等官，然亦潛通吐蕃，故謂之「兩面羌」。

translations.literal: Their tribes inherited prefect and other offices generation after generation, yet also secretly communicated with Tibet; therefore they were called "two-faced Qiang."
translations.idiomatic: Their tribes inherited prefectural offices generation after generation, yet also maintained secret ties with Tibet and were called the two-faced Qiang.

sentences.zh: 南詔蠻，本烏蠻之別種也，姓蒙氏。

translations.literal: The Nanzhao Man are originally a separate branch of the Wuman; their surname is the Meng clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanzhao tribes are a branch of the Wuman and bear the surname Meng.

sentences.zh: 蠻謂王為「詔。

translations.literal: The Man call a king "zhao."
translations.idiomatic: The Man word for king is zhao.

sentences.zh: 」自言哀牢之後，代居蒙舍州為渠帥，在漢永昌故郡東，姚州之西。

translations.literal: They say themselves to be descendants of Ailao, for generations dwelling in Mengshe Prefecture as tribal chiefs, east of the old Han commandery of Yongchang and west of Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They claim descent from Ailao and for generations have ruled as chiefs in Mengshe Prefecture, east of the old Han Yongchang commandery and west of Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先渠帥有六，自號「六詔」，兵力相埒，各有君長，無統帥。

translations.literal: Their former chiefs numbered six; they styled themselves the "Six Zhao"; military strength was equal; each had a lord and chief; there was no commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Six chiefs styled themselves the Six Zhao; their forces were evenly matched, each with its own ruler, and none held overall command.

sentences.zh: 蜀時為諸葛亮所征，皆臣服之。

translations.literal: In the Shu era they were campaigned against by Zhuge Liang and all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shu-Han era Zhuge Liang campaigned against them and they all submitted.

sentences.zh: 國初有蒙舍龍，生迦獨龐。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the dynasty there was Mengshe Long, who begot Jiadu Pang.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding there was Mengshe Long, who fathered Jiadu Pang.

sentences.zh: 迦獨生細奴邏，高宗時來朝。

translations.literal: Jiadu begot Xinuluo, who in Gaozong's time came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Jiadu's son Xinuluo came to court in Gaozong's reign.

sentences.zh: 細奴邏生邏盛，武後時來朝。

translations.literal: Xinuluo begot Luosheng, who in Empress Wu's time came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xinuluo's son Luosheng came to court under Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 其妻方娠，邏盛次姚州，聞妻生子，曰：「吾且有子，死於唐地足矣。

translations.literal: His wife was pregnant; Luosheng was staying at Ya Prefecture and heard his wife had borne a son, saying: "I am about to have a son; to die in Tang territory is enough.
translations.idiomatic: While his wife was pregnant, Luosheng was at Ya Prefecture; hearing she had borne a son, he said, "I am about to have a son—to die in Tang territory would be enough.

sentences.zh: 」子名曰盛邏皮。

translations.literal: The son was named Shengluopi.
translations.idiomatic: The child was named Shengluopi.

sentences.zh: 邏盛至京師，賜錦袍金帶歸國。

translations.literal: Luosheng reached the capital; he was granted a brocade robe and gold belt and returned to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Luosheng reached the capital, received a brocade robe and gold belt, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 開元初，邏盛死，子盛邏皮立。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, Luosheng died and his son Shengluopi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan Luosheng died and his son Shengluopi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 盛邏皮死，子皮邏閣立。

translations.literal: Shengluopi died; his son Piluoge succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengluopi died, his son Piluoge succeeded.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，詔授特進，封越國公，賜名曰歸義。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, an edict appointed him specially advanced, enfeoffed him as Duke of Yue, and granted the name Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Kaiyuan (738) he was appointed specially advanced, enfeoffed Duke of Yue, and given the name Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 其後破洱河蠻，以功策授雲南王。

translations.literal: Afterward he broke the Er River Man and for merit was appointed by patent King of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He later defeated the Er River tribes and was enfeoffed King of Yunnan for his merit.

sentences.zh: 歸義漸強盛，余五詔浸弱。

translations.literal: Guiyi gradually grew powerful; the remaining five zhao grew weak.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyi grew steadily stronger while the other five zhao weakened.

sentences.zh: 先是，劍南節度使王昱受歸義賂，奏六詔合為一詔。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jiannan frontier commissioner Wang Yu received bribes from Guiyi and memorialized that the six zhao be united into one zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jiannan commissioner Wang Yu, having accepted Guiyi's bribes, memorialized that the six zhao be united into one.

sentences.zh: 歸義既並五詔，服群蠻，破吐蕃之眾，兵日以驕大。

translations.literal: Guiyi having annexed the five zhao, made the mass of Man submit, and defeated Tibetan forces, his troops daily grew arrogant and great.
translations.idiomatic: Having annexed the five zhao, subdued the other tribes, and defeated Tibetan forces, Guiyi's power grew daily more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 每入覲，朝廷亦加禮異。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered court audience, the court also added special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to court the throne treated him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，徙居大和城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he moved his residence to Taihe city.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Kaiyuan (739) he moved his capital to Taihe.

sentences.zh: 天寶四載，歸義遣孫鳳迦異來朝，授鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao, Guiyi sent his grandson Feng Jiayi to court; he was appointed director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianbao (745) Guiyi sent his grandson Feng Jiayi to court and he was appointed director of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 歸國，恩賜甚厚，歸義意望亦高。

translations.literal: On returning to his state, favors and gifts were very generous; Guiyi's ambitions were also high.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home richly rewarded, and Guiyi's ambitions rose accordingly.

sentences.zh: 時劍南節度使章仇兼瓊遣使至雲南，與歸義言語不相得，歸義常銜之。

translations.literal: At the time the Jiannan frontier commissioner Zhang Chou Jianqiong sent envoys to Yunnan; he and Guiyi did not get along in speech, and Guiyi constantly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiannan commissioner Zhang Chou Jianqiong sent envoys to Yunnan whose dealings with Guiyi were abrasive, and Guiyi bore a lasting grudge.

sentences.zh: 七年，歸義卒，詔立子閣羅鳳襲雲南王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Guiyi died; an edict installed his son Geluofeng to succeed as King of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianbao (748) Guiyi died; an edict installed his son Geluofeng as King of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 無何，鮮于仲通為劍南節度使，張虔陀為雲南太守。

translations.literal: Before long, Xianyu Zhongtong became Jiannan frontier commissioner and Zhang Qiantuo became prefect of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xianyu Zhongtong became Jiannan commissioner and Zhang Qiantuo prefect of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 仲通褊急寡謀，虔陀矯詐，待之不以禮。

translations.literal: Zhongtong was narrow, impatient, and lacking in strategy; Qiantuo was crafty and deceitful; they did not treat him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong was narrow-minded and rash, Qiantuo deceitful, and neither treated Geluofeng with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 舊事，南詔常與其妻子謁見都督，虔陀皆私之。

translations.literal: By old practice, Nanzhao often came with wife and children to pay respects to the area commander; Qiantuo took them all for himself.
translations.idiomatic: By custom Nanzhao came with his wife and children to call on the area commander; Qiantuo appropriated them for himself.

sentences.zh: 有所征求，閣羅鳳多不應，虔陀遣人罵辱之，仍密奏其罪惡。

translations.literal: When there were demands, Geluofeng mostly did not comply; Qiantuo sent men to revile and insult him and still secretly memorialized his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: When demands were made Geluofeng often refused; Qiantuo sent men to revile him and secretly memorialized his offenses.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳忿怨，因發兵反攻，圍虔陀，殺之，時天寶九年也。

translations.literal: Geluofeng was resentful and angry; he therefore raised troops to counterattack, besieged Qiantuo, and killed him—it was the ninth year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng, enraged, raised troops, besieged Qiantuo, and killed him in the ninth year of Tianbao (750).

sentences.zh: 明年，仲通率兵出戎、巂州。

translations.literal: The next year, Zhongtong led troops out from Rong and Xi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhongtong led troops out from Rong and Xi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳遣使謝罪，仍與雲南錄事參軍姜如芝俱來，請還其所虜掠，且言：「吐蕃大兵壓境，若不許，當歸命吐蕃，雲南之地，非唐所有也。

translations.literal: Geluofeng sent envoys to apologize for guilt, and still together with the Yunnan registrar Jiang Ruzhi came, requesting return of those they had captured and plundered, and moreover said: "Tibetan great armies press the border; if not permitted, I shall submit to Tibet—Yunnan's land is not Tang's possession."
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng sent envoys to apologize, coming with the Yunnan registrar Jiang Ruzhi to request the return of captives and saying: "Tibetan armies press the border; if you refuse, I must submit to Tibet, for Yunnan is no longer Tang territory."

sentences.zh: 」仲通不許，囚其使，進兵逼大和城，為南詔所敗。

translations.literal: Zhongtong did not permit it, imprisoned their envoys, advanced troops pressing Taihe city, and was defeated by Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongtong refused, imprisoned the envoys, advanced on Taihe, and was defeated by Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 自是閣羅鳳北臣吐蕃。

translations.literal: From this time Geluofeng northward became subject to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Geluofeng submitted to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃令閣羅鳳為贊普鐘，號曰東帝，給以金印。
