translations.literal: Tibet made Geluofeng Eastern Brother of the Zanpu, styled Eastern Emperor, and gave him a gold seal.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet made Geluofeng Eastern Brother of the Zanpu, styled Eastern Emperor, and granted him a gold seal.

sentences.zh: 蠻謂弟為「鐘」，時天寶十一年也。

translations.literal: The Man call a younger brother "zhong"; it was the eleventh year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: The Man word for younger brother is zhong; this was in the eleventh year of Tianbao (752).

sentences.zh: 十二年，劍南節度使楊國忠執國政，仍奏征天下兵，俾留後、侍御史李宓將十余萬，輦餉者在外。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Jiannan frontier commissioner Yang Guozhong held state power and still memorialized to levy troops from all the realm, ordering the acting commissioner and attendant censor Li Mi to command more than a hundred thousand, with those hauling provisions outside.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianbao (753) Yang Guozhong, holding state power, memorialized for troops from across the empire; the acting commissioner Li Mi led more than a hundred thousand men, with supply convoys strung out behind.

sentences.zh: 涉海，瘴死者相屬於路，天下始騷然苦之。

translations.literal: Crossing marshes, those who died of miasma followed one another along the road; the realm began to be disturbed and suffer from it.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing pestilential marshes, the dead lined the roads, and the empire began to groan under the burden.

sentences.zh: 宓復敗於大和城北，死者十八、九。

translations.literal: Mi again was defeated north of Taihe city; eighty or ninety percent died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was again defeated north of Taihe; eight or nine in ten of his men perished.

sentences.zh: 會安祿山反，閣羅鳳乘釁攻陷巂州及會同軍，西復降尋傳蠻。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Geluofeng seized the opportunity to attack and take Xi Prefecture and the Huitong army; westward he again made the Xunchuan Man submit.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Geluofeng seized the moment to capture Xi Prefecture and the Huitong garrison and subdue the Xunchuan tribes to the west.

sentences.zh: 大歷十四年，閣羅鳳子鳳迦異先閣羅鳳死，立迦異子，是為異牟尋。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Dali, Geluofeng's son Feng Jiayi died before Geluofeng; his son was installed—this was Yimouxun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Dali (779) Geluofeng's son Feng Jiayi predeceased his father; Feng Jiayi's son Yimouxun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 頗知書，有才智，善撫其眾。

translations.literal: He was quite versed in books, had talent and wisdom, and was skilled in soothing his multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He was literate, talented, and skilled at winning the loyalty of his people.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃役賦南蠻重數，又奪諸蠻險地立城堡，歲征兵以助鎮防，牟尋益厭苦之。

translations.literal: Tibet's corvée and levies on the southern Man were heavy and repeated; they also seized the strategic lands of the various Man to erect fortresses and each year conscripted troops to aid frontier defense—Mouxun grew ever more weary and bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet imposed heavy levies on the southern tribes, seized their strategic lands for fortresses, and conscripted troops yearly for frontier defense—Yimouxun grew ever more resentful.

sentences.zh: 有鄭回者，本相州人，天寶中舉明經，授巂州西瀘縣令。

translations.literal: There was one Zheng Hui, originally a man of Xiang Prefecture; in Tianbao he passed the classics examination and was appointed magistrate of Xilu county in Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Zheng Hui from Xiang Prefecture who passed the classics examination in the Tianbao era and was appointed magistrate of Xilu in Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 巂州陷，為所虜。

translations.literal: When Xi Prefecture fell, he was captured by them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Prefecture fell he was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 閣羅鳳以回有儒學，更名曰蠻利。

translations.literal: Geluofeng, because Hui had Confucian learning, changed his name to Manli.
translations.idiomatic: Geluofeng, finding Hui learned in the classics, renamed him Manli.

sentences.zh: 甚愛重之，命教鳳迦異。

translations.literal: He greatly cherished and esteemed him and ordered him to teach Feng Jiayi.
translations.idiomatic: He valued him highly and appointed him tutor to Feng Jiayi.

sentences.zh: 及異牟尋立，又命教其子尋夢湊。

translations.literal: When Yimouxun succeeded, again he ordered him to teach his son Xunmengchou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yimouxun succeeded, he appointed Manli tutor to his son Xunmengchou as well.

sentences.zh: 回久為蠻師，凡授學，雖牟尋、夢湊，回得箠撻，故牟尋以下皆嚴憚之。

translations.literal: Hui long served as Man teacher; in all instruction, even Mouxun and Mengchou—Hui could flog and beat them; therefore from Mouxun downward all strictly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Manli had long served as their teacher and would beat even Yimouxun and Xunmengchou in lessons, so all feared him.

sentences.zh: 蠻謂相為清平官，凡置六人。

translations.literal: The Man call a minister qingpingguan; in all six are appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The Man term for minister is qingpingguan; six are appointed.

sentences.zh: 牟尋以回為清平官，事皆咨之，秉政用事。

translations.literal: Mouxun made Hui a qingpingguan; on all affairs he was consulted, holding government and wielding power.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun made Manli a qingpingguan and consulted him on all affairs; he held real power.

sentences.zh: 余清平官五人，事回卑謹，或有過，回輒撻之。

translations.literal: The remaining five qingpingguan served Hui humbly and respectfully; if there were faults, Hui would beat them.
translations.idiomatic: The other five qingpingguan served Manli humbly; when they erred he beat them.

sentences.zh: 回嘗言於牟尋曰：「自昔南詔嘗款附中國，中國尚禮義，以惠養為務，無所求取。

translations.literal: Hui once said to Mouxun: "From of old Nanzhao has sincerely attached to China; China esteems ritual and righteousness, taking generous nurturing as its task, seeking nothing in return.
translations.idiomatic: Manli once told Yimouxun: "Nanzhao has long been loyal to China, which esteems ritual and righteousness and nurtures its allies without demanding tribute.

sentences.zh: 今棄蕃歸唐，無遠戍之勞、重稅之困，利莫大焉。

translations.literal: Now to abandon Tibet and return to Tang—without the toil of distant garrison service or the hardship of heavy taxes—the benefit is greatest."
translations.idiomatic: To abandon Tibet and return to Tang now would free you from distant garrisons and heavy levies—the benefit could hardly be greater."

sentences.zh: 」牟尋善其言，謀內附者十余年矣。

translations.literal: Mouxun approved his words and had plotted internal submission for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun approved and had been plotting submission to Tang for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 會劍南西川節度使韋臯招撫諸蠻，苴烏星、虜望等歸化，微聞牟尋之意，因令蠻寓書於牟尋，且招懷之，時貞元四年也。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jiannan West River frontier commissioner Wei Gao recruited and soothed the various Man; Juwuxing, Luwang, and others submitted; he faintly heard Mouxun's intent and therefore had a Man lodge a letter with Mouxun and moreover win him over—it was the fourth year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Gao, commissioner of Jiannan West River, was winning over the tribes and Juwuxing and Luwang submitted, he caught wind of Yimouxun's intentions and had a Man deliver a letter of outreach—it was the fourth year of Zhenyuan (788).

sentences.zh: 七年，又遣間使持書喻之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, again he sent a secret envoy bearing a letter to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenyuan (791) he again sent a secret envoy with a letter.

sentences.zh: 道出磨些蠻，其魁主潛告吐蕃，使至雲南。

translations.literal: The route passed through the Mosuo Man; their chief secretly informed Tibet, and the envoy reached Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The route passed through Mosuo territory whose chief secretly informed Tibet, and the envoy reached Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃已知之，令詰牟尋。

translations.literal: Tibet already knew of it and ordered Mouxun interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet learned of it and summoned Yimouxun for questioning.

sentences.zh: 牟尋懼，因紿吐蕃曰：「唐使，本蠻也，韋臯許其求歸，無他謀。

translations.literal: Mouxun was afraid and therefore deceived Tibet, saying: "The Tang envoy was originally a Man; Wei Gao permitted his request to return—there is no other plot."
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun, afraid, deceived Tibet: "The Tang envoy was a Man whom Wei Gao allowed to return home—there is no other plot."

sentences.zh: 」遂執送吐蕃。

translations.literal: He was then seized and sent to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was seized and handed over to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃益疑之，多召南詔大臣之子為質，牟尋愈怨。

translations.literal: Tibet grew more suspicious and summoned many sons of Nanzhao great ministers as hostages; Mouxun's resentment increased.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet grew more suspicious and took many sons of Nanzhao ministers as hostages, deepening Yimouxun's resentment.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，牟尋乃與酋長定計遣使：趙莫羅眉由兩川，楊大和堅由黔中，或由安南。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year, Mouxun then with chieftains fixed a plan and sent envoys: Zhao Moluomei by the two rivers, Yang Dahejian by Qianzhong, or by Annan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the ninth year of Zhenyuan (793) Yimouxun and his chiefs sent envoys by three routes: Zhao Moluomei through the two rivers, Yang Dahejian through Qianzhong, and another through Annan.

sentences.zh: 使凡三輩，致書與韋臯，各賫生金丹砂為贄。

translations.literal: The envoys in all three parties brought letters to Wei Gao, each carrying raw gold and cinnabar as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Three missions bore letters to Wei Gao, each carrying raw gold and cinnabar as gifts.

sentences.zh: 三分前臯所與牟尋書，各持其一為信。

translations.literal: They divided the letter formerly given by Gao to Mouxun into three parts; each held one as credential.
translations.idiomatic: They divided among them a letter Wei Gao had earlier given Yimouxun, each carrying a third as proof.

sentences.zh: 歲中，三使皆至京師，且曰：「牟尋請歸大國，永為籓國。

translations.literal: Within the year, all three envoys reached the capital and moreover said: "Mouxun requests to return to the great state and forever be a feudatory state."
translations.idiomatic: Within the year all three envoys reached the capital with the message: "Yimouxun asks to return to the great empire and be its vassal forever."

sentences.zh: 所獻生金，以喻向北之意如金也；

translations.literal: The raw gold presented was to symbolize the intent toward the north, like gold;
translations.idiomatic: The raw gold they offered symbolized their turn toward the north, steadfast as gold;

sentences.zh: 丹砂，示其赤心耳。

translations.literal: cinnabar showed their red heart alone.
translations.idiomatic: the cinnabar showed their loyal hearts.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉之，乃賜牟尋詔書，因命韋臯遣使以觀其情。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this and bestowed on Mouxun an imperial edict, and ordered Wei Gao to send envoys to observe his sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, granted Yimouxun an imperial edict, and ordered Wei Gao to send envoys to ascertain his intentions.

sentences.zh: 臯遂命巡官崔佐時至牟尋所都陽苴咩城，南去太和城十餘里，東北至成都二千四百里，東至安南如至成都，通水陸行。

translations.literal: Gao then ordered the touring officer Cui Zuoshi to reach Mouxun's capital Yangjuemie city, more than ten li south of Taihe city, two thousand four hundred li northeast to Chengdu, and east to Annan as to Chengdu—accessible by water and land routes.
translations.idiomatic: Gao dispatched the touring officer Cui Zuoshi to Yimouxun's capital Yangjuemie, a little over ten li south of Taihe—two thousand four hundred li northeast of Chengdu and as far east as Annan, reachable by water and land alike.

sentences.zh: 是時也，吐蕃使數百人，先佐時在南詔。

translations.literal: At that time several hundred Tibetan envoys were already in Nanzhao before Zuoshi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time several hundred Tibetan envoys were already in Nanzhao when Zuoshi arrived.

sentences.zh: 牟尋悉召諸種落與議歸化，或未畢至，未敢公言，密令佐時稱牂牁使，衣以牂牁服而入。

translations.literal: Mouxun had summoned all tribes and clans to discuss submission; some had not yet fully arrived and he dared not speak openly; he secretly ordered Zuoshi to call himself a Zangge envoy and enter wearing Zangge dress.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun had summoned all the tribes to discuss submission, but not all had yet arrived and he dared not speak openly; he secretly asked Zuoshi to pose as a Zangge envoy and enter in Zangge dress.

sentences.zh: 佐時不肯，曰：「我大唐使，安得服小夷之服。

translations.literal: Zuoshi refused, saying: "I am an envoy of Great Tang—how could I wear the dress of petty barbarians?"
translations.idiomatic: Zuoshi refused: "I am an envoy of Great Tang—how could I wear the garb of petty tribes?"

sentences.zh: 」牟尋不得已，乃夜迎佐時，設位陳燈燭。

translations.literal: Mouxun had no choice; he therefore received Zuoshi by night, set out seats, and displayed lamps and candles.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun had no choice but to receive Zuoshi by night, setting out seats and lamps.

sentences.zh: 佐時乃大宣詔書。

translations.literal: Zuoshi then loudly proclaimed the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zuoshi then proclaimed the imperial edict aloud.

sentences.zh: 牟尋恐吐蕃知，顧左右無色，而業已歸唐，久之，歔欷流涕，皆俯伏受命。

translations.literal: Mouxun feared Tibet would learn of it and glanced at those beside him, who were pale; yet having already submitted to Tang, after a long while he sobbed with tears flowing, and all bowed prostrate to receive the command.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun, fearing Tibet would learn of it, glanced at his attendants, who turned pale; but having already committed to Tang, he wept at length, and all prostrated themselves to receive the command.

sentences.zh: 其明年正月，異牟尋使其子閣勸及清平官等與佐時，盟於點蒼山神祠。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Yimouxun sent his son Gequan and the qingpingguan and others with Zuoshi to covenant at the shrine of the Diancang Mountain spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Yimouxun sent his son Gequan, the qingpingguan, and others to swear alliance with Zuoshi at the shrine of the Diancang Mountain spirit.

sentences.zh: 盟書一藏於神室，一沈於西洱河，一置祖廟，一以進天子。

translations.literal: One copy of the covenant text was stored in the spirit chamber, one sunk in the Western Er River, one placed in the ancestral temple, and one presented to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: One copy of the covenant was stored in the spirit shrine, one sunk in the Western Er River, one placed in the ancestral temple, and one sent to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 閣勸即尋夢湊也。

translations.literal: Gequan was Xunmengchou.
translations.idiomatic: Gequan was Xunmengchou.

sentences.zh: 鄭回見佐時，多所指導，故佐時探得其情。

translations.literal: Zheng Hui met Zuoshi and gave much guidance; therefore Zuoshi probed and obtained his true situation.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hui met Zuoshi and gave much guidance, enabling him to grasp the full situation.

sentences.zh: 乃請牟尋斬吐蕃使數人，以示歸唐。

translations.literal: He then requested Mouxun execute several Tibetan envoys to show submission to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Yimouxun to execute several Tibetan envoys as proof of submission to Tang.

sentences.zh: 又得其吐蕃所與金印。

translations.literal: He also obtained the gold seal Tibet had given them.
translations.idiomatic: He also obtained the gold seal Tibet had granted them.

sentences.zh: 牟尋尋遣佐時歸，仍刻金契以獻。

translations.literal: Mouxun soon sent Zuoshi back and still carved a gold covenant to present.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun soon sent Zuoshi home and presented a carved gold covenant.

sentences.zh: 閣勸賦詩以餞之。

translations.literal: Gequan composed a poem to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: Gequan composed a farewell poem for him.

sentences.zh: 牟尋乃去吐蕃所立帝號，私於佐時，請復南詔舊名。

translations.literal: Mouxun then removed the imperial title Tibet had installed and privately told Zuoshi, requesting restoration of Nanzhao's old name.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun then cast off the imperial title Tibet had imposed and privately asked Zuoshi to restore Nanzhao's former name.

sentences.zh: 佐時與盟訖，留二旬有六日而歸。

translations.literal: When Zuoshi had finished the covenant, he remained twenty-six days and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After completing the alliance Zuoshi stayed twenty-six days and returned.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃因爭北庭，與回鶻大戰，死傷頗眾。

translations.literal: Earlier, because of contesting Beiting, Tibet fought a great battle with the Uyghurs and casualties were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tibet had fought the Uyghurs over Beiting and suffered heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 乃征兵於牟尋，須萬人。

translations.literal: They then conscripted troops from Mouxun, requiring ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: They then demanded ten thousand troops from Yimouxun.

sentences.zh: 牟尋既定計歸我，欲因征兵以襲之。

translations.literal: Mouxun having already fixed his plan to return to us, wished to use the conscription to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun, having already resolved to return to Tang, planned to use the conscription as a pretext to strike Tibet.

sentences.zh: 乃示寡弱，謂吐蕃曰：「蠻軍素少，僅可發三千人。

translations.literal: He therefore showed weakness and fewness, telling Tibet: "Man troops have always been few; only three thousand can be sent."
translations.idiomatic: He feigned weakness, telling Tibet: "Our forces have always been few—we can send only three thousand men."

sentences.zh: 」吐蕃少之，請益至五千，乃許。

translations.literal: Tibet considered it too few and requested increase to five thousand; he then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet protested the number was too small and pressed for five thousand; he agreed.

sentences.zh: 牟尋遽遣兵五千人戍吐蕃，乃自將數萬踵其後，晝夜兼行，乘其無備，大破吐蕃於神川。

translations.literal: Mouxun swiftly sent five thousand troops to garrison for Tibet, then personally led tens of thousands following behind, traveling day and night together, seizing their lack of preparation and greatly defeating Tibet at Shenchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun sent five thousand men to garrison for Tibet, then personally led tens of thousands in their wake, marching day and night, and routing the Tibetans at Shenchuan by surprise.

sentences.zh: 遂斷鐵橋，遣使告捷。

translations.literal: He then severed the Iron Bridge and sent envoys to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: He severed the Iron Bridge and sent envoys to report victory.

sentences.zh: 且請韋臯使閱其所虜獲及城堡，以取信焉。

translations.literal: Moreover he requested Wei Gao send someone to inspect what they had captured and the fortresses, to obtain credence.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Wei Gao to send someone to inspect the captives and fortresses as proof.

sentences.zh: 時韋臯上言：「牟尋收鐵橋已來城壘一十六，擒其王五人，降其眾十余萬。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Gao memorialized: "Mouxun recovered sixteen fortresses from the Iron Bridge onward, captured five of their kings, and made more than a hundred thousand of their multitude submit."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao memorialized: "Yimouxun has taken sixteen fortresses from the Iron Bridge onward, captured five Tibetan kings, and received the submission of more than a hundred thousand men."

sentences.zh: 」以祠部郎中兼御史中丞袁滋持節冊南詔，仍賜牟尋印，鑄用黃金，以銀為窠。

translations.literal: The director of sacrifices Yuan Zi, concurrently censor-in-chief, was sent with credentials to enfeoff Nanzhao; Mouxun was still granted a seal, cast using gold with silver for the socket.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zi of the Sacrifices Bureau, concurrently censor-in-chief, was sent to enfeoff Nanzhao; Yimouxun was granted a seal cast in gold with a silver socket.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「貞元冊南詔印。

translations.literal: The inscription read: "Zhenyuan Enfeoffment Seal of Nanzhao."
translations.idiomatic: The inscription read: "Zhenyuan Enfeoffment Seal of Nanzhao."

sentences.zh: 」先是，韋臯奏南詔前遣清平官尹仇寬獻所受吐蕃印五，二用黃金，今賜請以黃金，從蠻夷所重，傳示無窮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Gao had memorialized that Nanzhao's former dispatch of the qingpingguan Yin Qiukuan presented five seals received from Tibet, two of gold; now in bestowing, he requested gold be used, following what the Man barbarians esteem, to be transmitted and displayed without end.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wei Gao had reported that the qingpingguan Yin Qiukuan had presented five seals received from Tibet, two of gold; he now requested that the new seal be of gold as well, in keeping with what the tribes value, to be handed down forever.

sentences.zh: 從臯之請也。

translations.literal: This followed Gao's request.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted Gao's request.

sentences.zh: 十年八月，遣使蒙湊羅棟及尹仇寬來獻鐸槊、浪人劍及吐蕃印八紐。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year, they sent envoys Meng Chouluodong and Yin Qiukuan to present iron maces, wave-man swords, and eight Tibetan seal cords.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the tenth year of Zhenyuan (794) they sent Meng Chouluodong and Yin Qiukuan with iron maces, wave-man swords, and eight Tibetan seals.

sentences.zh: 湊羅棟，牟尋之弟也，錫賚甚厚，以尹仇寬為檢校左散騎常侍，余各授官有差。

translations.literal: Chouluodong was Mouxun's younger brother; rewards and gifts were very generous; Yin Qiukuan was made acting left regular attendant of the Palace Steeds; the rest were each granted offices according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chouluodong was Yimouxun's brother and was richly rewarded; Yin Qiukuan was appointed acting left regular attendant of the Palace Steeds, and the others received offices in due order.

sentences.zh: 俄又封尹仇寬為高溪郡王。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Yin Qiukuan was enfeoffed as king of Gaoxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yin Qiukuan was enfeoffed King of Gaoxi.

sentences.zh: 十一年三月，遣清平官尹輔酋隨袁滋來朝。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eleventh year, they sent the qingpingguan Yin Fushou following Yuan Zi to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eleventh year (795) the qingpingguan Yin Fushou came to court with Yuan Zi.

sentences.zh: 又得先沒蕃將衛景升、韓演等，並南詔所獲吐蕃將帥俘馘百人至京師。

translations.literal: They also obtained the former Tang generals lost to Tibet Wei Jingsheng and Han Yan and others, together with a hundred Tibetan generals and commanders captured by Nanzhao, brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They also recovered the former Tang generals Wei Jingsheng and Han Yan, lost to Tibet, together with a hundred Tibetan officers captured by Nanzhao, all brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 湊羅棟歸國，在道而卒，贈右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Chouluodong returned to his state and died on the road; he was posthumously granted right regular attendant of the Palace Steeds.
translations.idiomatic: Chouluodong died on the road home and was posthumously made right regular attendant of the Palace Steeds.

sentences.zh: 授尹輔酋檢校太子詹事兼御史中丞，余亦差次授官。

translations.literal: Yin Fushou was appointed acting grand mentor of the heir apparent and concurrently censor-in-chief; the rest also received offices in descending order.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Fushou was appointed acting grand mentor of the heir apparent and censor-in-chief; the others received offices in due order.

sentences.zh: 又降敕書賜異牟尋及子閣勸，清平官鄭回、尹仇寬等各一書，書左列中書三官宣奉行，復舊制也。

translations.literal: Imperial letters were also sent down bestowing on Yimouxun and his son Gequan, the qingpingguan Zheng Hui, Yin Qiukuan, and each one letter; on the left of the letter the three officials of the Secretariat were listed proclaiming execution—restoring the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial letters were sent to Yimouxun, his son Gequan, and the qingpingguan Zheng Hui and Yin Qiukuan, each bearing on the left the names of the three Secretariat officials proclaiming execution—the old format restored.

sentences.zh: 九月，異牟尋遣使獻馬六十匹。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yimouxun sent envoys presenting sixty horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yimouxun sent sixty horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二年，韋臯於雅州會野路招收得投降蠻首領高萬唐等六十九人，戶約七千，兼萬唐等先受吐蕃金字告身五十片。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Wei Gao at Yazhou on the Huiye road recruited and received the surrender of Man chieftains Gao Wantang and sixty-nine others, households numbering about seven thousand, together with fifty golden-character patents of office formerly received by Wantang and others from Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Wei Gao at Yazhou on the Huiye road received the submission of sixty-nine Man chieftains including Gao Wantang, about seven thousand households, along with fifty golden patents of office they had earlier received from Tibet.

sentences.zh: 十四年，異牟尋遣酋望大將軍王丘各等賀正，兼獻方物。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Yimouxun sent the chieftain-general Wang Qiuge and others to congratulate the New Year and moreover present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Yimouxun sent the chieftain-general Wang Qiuge and others for the New Year audience with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月旦，上御含元殿受南詔朝賀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the nineteenth year, the emperor attended at the Hanyuan Hall to receive Nanzhao's court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan (803) the emperor received Nanzhao's homage in the Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 以其使楊鏌龍武為試太仆少卿，授黎州廓清道蠻首領襲恭化郡王劉誌寧試太常卿。

translations.literal: Their envoy Yang Minglongwu was made acting vice minister of the Imperial Stud; the Man chieftain of Lizhou Kuoqing Road who succeeded as King of Gonghua commandery Liu Zhining was appointed acting minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoy Yang Minglongwu was appointed acting vice minister of the Imperial Stud, and the Man chieftain Liu Zhining of Lizhou Kuoqing Road, who had succeeded as King of Gonghua, was appointed acting minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 二十年，南詔遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Nanzhao sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Zhenyuan (804) Nanzhao sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 元和二年八月，遣使鄧傍傳來朝，授試殿中監。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Yuanhe, they sent the envoy Deng Bangchuan to court; he was appointed acting director of the Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Yuanhe (807) they sent the envoy Deng Bangchuan to court and he was appointed acting director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，以異牟尋卒，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year, because Yimouxun died, court was suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Yuanhe (808) court mourning was observed for three days upon Yimouxun's death.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，以太常少卿武少儀充吊祭使，仍冊牟尋之子驃信苴蒙閣勸為南詔王，仍命鑄「元和冊南詔印」。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, the vice minister of Ceremonies Wu Shaoyi was made condolence envoy and still enfeoffed Mouxun's son the piaoxin Jumeng Gequan as king of Nanzhao; he was still ordered to cast the "Yuanhe Enfeoffment Seal of Nanzhao."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Yuanhe (809) Wu Shaoyi, vice minister of Ceremonies, was sent as condolence envoy to enfeoff Mouxun's son, the piaoxin Jumeng Gequan, as king of Nanzhao and to cast the Yuanhe Enfeoffment Seal of Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 七年十月，皆遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year, all sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the seventh year of Yuanhe (812) they all sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月，以龍蒙盛卒，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year, because Longmengsheng died, court was suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year of Yuanhe (816) court mourning was observed for three days upon Longmengsheng's death.

sentences.zh: 遣使來請冊立其君長。

translations.literal: They sent envoys requesting enfeoffment and installation of their lord and chief.
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys requesting investiture of their new ruler.

sentences.zh: 以少府少監李銑充冊立吊祭使，左贊善大夫許堯佐副之。

translations.literal: The vice director of the Palace Workshops Li Xian was made enfeoffment and condolence envoy; the left aide to the heir apparent Xu Yaozuo served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, vice director of the Palace Workshops, was sent as investiture and condolence envoy with Xu Yaozuo, left aide to the heir apparent, as deputy.

sentences.zh: 十二年至十五年，比年遣使來朝，或年內二三至者。

translations.literal: From the twelfth to the fifteenth year, year after year they sent envoys to court, sometimes two or three arrivals within a year.
translations.idiomatic: From the twelfth to the fifteenth year they sent envoys annually, sometimes two or three missions in a single year.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，其王蒙嵯顛以表自陳請罪，兼疏元穎過失。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, its king Mengcuandian by memorial confessed guilt himself and moreover detailed Yuan Ying's faults.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year King Mengcuandian submitted a memorial confessing guilt and detailing Yuan Ying's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 國家方事柔遠，尋釋其罪，復遣使來朝。

translations.literal: The state was then pursuing gentle treatment of the distant; soon his guilt was released and again they sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: The court, pursuing a policy of gentle treatment of distant peoples, soon pardoned him and again received his envoys.

sentences.zh: 五年、八年，亦遣使來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fifth and eighth years, again they sent envoys to present local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth and eighth years they again sent envoys with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 開成四年、五年，會昌二年，皆遣使來朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth and fifth years of Kaicheng and the second year of Huichang, all sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth and fifth years of Kaicheng (839–840), and the second year of Huichang (842), they all sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 驃國，在永昌故郡南二千餘里，去上都一萬四千里。

translations.literal: The state of Pyu is more than two thousand li south of the old commandery of Yongchang, fourteen thousand li from the upper capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pyu lies more than two thousand li south of the old Yongchang commandery, fourteen thousand li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 其國境，東西三千里，南北三千五百里。

translations.literal: Its state's territory is three thousand li east and west, three thousand five hundred li north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory measures three thousand li east to west and three thousand five hundred li north to south.

sentences.zh: 東鄰真臘國，西接東天竺國，南盡溟海，北通南詔些樂城界，東北拒陽苴咩城六千八百里。

translations.literal: East it neighbors Chenla; west it connects with Eastern India; south it reaches the dark sea; north it communicates with Nanzhao's Xile city border; northeast it is six thousand eight hundred li from Yangjuemie city.
translations.idiomatic: It borders Chenla on the east and Eastern India on the west, reaches the southern ocean, adjoins Nanzhao's Xile frontier on the north, and lies six thousand eight hundred li northeast of Yangjuemie.

sentences.zh: 往來通聘迦羅婆提等二十國，役屬者道林王等九城，食境土者羅君潛等二百九十部落。

translations.literal: Coming and going in diplomatic exchange with twenty states such as Kalapati; nine cities such as Daolinwang under service and subordination; two hundred ninety tribes such as Luo Junqian consuming its territory.
translations.idiomatic: It exchanges embassies with twenty states including Kalapati, commands nine cities including Daolinwang, and holds two hundred ninety tribes including Luo Junqian within its domain.

sentences.zh: 其王姓困沒長，名摩羅惹。

translations.literal: Its king's surname is Kunmozhang; his name is Moluore.
translations.idiomatic: The king's surname is Kunmozhang and his name Moluore.

sentences.zh: 其國相名摩訶思那。

translations.literal: Its state's chancellor is named Mohesina.
translations.idiomatic: The state chancellor is named Mohesina.

sentences.zh: 其王近適則舁以金繩床，遠適則乘象。

translations.literal: For near journeys the king is carried on a golden cord bed; for distant journeys he rides an elephant.
translations.idiomatic: For short journeys the king is carried on a gold-cord litter; for long journeys he rides an elephant.

sentences.zh: 嬪妹甚眾，常數百人。

translations.literal: Consorts and younger sisters are very many, constantly numbering several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: His consorts and sisters number several hundred.

sentences.zh: 其羅城構以專甃，周一百六十里，濠岸亦構專，相傳本是舍利佛城。

translations.literal: Its outer city is built with brick tiling, one hundred sixty li in circumference; the moat banks are also built with brick—it is handed down that this was originally the city of the Buddha relic.
translations.idiomatic: Its outer city is built of brick, one hundred sixty li in circumference, with brick moat banks as well—tradition holds it was originally the city of the Buddha relic.

sentences.zh: 城內有居人數萬家，佛寺百余區。

translations.literal: Within the city are several tens of thousands of resident households and more than a hundred Buddhist temple compounds.
translations.idiomatic: Within the walls live tens of thousands of households and more than a hundred Buddhist monasteries.

sentences.zh: 其堂宇皆錯以金銀，塗以丹彩，地以紫鑛，覆以錦罽。

translations.literal: Their halls and chambers are all inlaid with gold and silver, painted with cinnabar colors, floored with purple ore, and covered with brocade rugs.
translations.idiomatic: Their halls are inlaid with gold and silver, painted in cinnabar, floored with purple stone, and covered with brocade rugs.

sentences.zh: 其俗好生惡殺。

translations.literal: Their custom cherishes life and hates killing.
translations.idiomatic: They cherish life and abhor killing.

sentences.zh: 其土宜菽粟稻梁，無麻麥。

translations.literal: Its soil suits beans, millet, rice, and sorghum; there is no hemp or wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The soil supports beans, millet, rice, and sorghum, but not hemp or wheat.

sentences.zh: 其理無刑名桎梏之具，犯罪者以竹五十本束之，復犯者撻其背，數止五，輕者止三，殺人者戮之。

translations.literal: In their governance there are no instruments of punishment and shackles; offenders are bound with fifty bamboo staves; repeat offenders are flogged on the back, the count stopping at five, light cases stopping at three; killers are executed.
translations.idiomatic: They have no penal instruments or shackles; offenders are bound with fifty bamboo staves, repeat offenders flogged on the back—five strokes for serious cases, three for minor—and murderers are executed.

sentences.zh: 男女七歲則落發，止寺舍，依桑門，至二十不悟佛理，乃復長發為居人。

translations.literal: Boys and girls at seven then shave the head, stay in temple quarters, and follow monks; reaching twenty without comprehending Buddhist principles, they then grow hair long again and become residents.
translations.idiomatic: At seven boys and girls shave their heads and live in monasteries as novices; if by twenty they have not grasped Buddhist doctrine, they let their hair grow and return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 其衣服悉以白赩為朝霞，繞腰而已。

translations.literal: Their clothing is all white xi cloth as dawn-glow, wrapped about the waist alone.
translations.idiomatic: Their clothing is white cotton cloth wrapped about the waist.

sentences.zh: 不衣繒帛，雲出於蠶，為其傷生故也。

translations.literal: They do not wear silk and brocade, saying it comes from the silkworm and therefore harms life.
translations.idiomatic: They do not wear silk, holding that it harms life because it comes from silkworms.

sentences.zh: 君臣父子長幼有序。

translations.literal: Ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger have proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and subject, parent and child, elder and younger observe proper order.

sentences.zh: 華言謂之驃，自謂突羅成阇婆，人謂之徒裏掘。

translations.literal: In Chinese speech it is called Pyu; they call themselves Tulachengqiepo; people call them Tulijue.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese calls them Pyu; they call themselves Tulachengqiepo; others call them Tulijue.

sentences.zh: 古未嘗通中國。

translations.literal: Of old they never communicated with China.
translations.idiomatic: They had never before had contact with China.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，其王聞南詔異牟尋歸附，心慕之。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan, its king heard that Nanzhao's Yimouxun had submitted and his heart admired this.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan its king heard that Nanzhao's Yimouxun had submitted to Tang and admired the example.

sentences.zh: 八年，乃遣其弟悉利移因南詔重譯來朝，又獻其國樂凡十曲，與樂工三十五人俱。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he then sent his younger brother Xilijiao through Nanzhao's double translation to court, and moreover presented ten pieces of his state's music, together with thirty-five musicians.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan (792) he sent his brother Xilijiao to court through Nanzhao's interpreters, presenting ten pieces of Pyu music with thirty-five musicians.

sentences.zh: 樂曲皆演釋氏經論之詞意。

translations.literal: The musical pieces all perform the words and meaning of Buddhist sutras and treatises.
translations.idiomatic: The pieces all set to music the words of Buddhist sutras and treatises.

sentences.zh: 尋以悉利移為試太仆卿。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Xilijiao was made acting minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xilijiao was appointed acting minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：禹畫九州，周分六服，斷長補短，止方七千。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Yu delineated the Nine Provinces; Zhou divided the Six Domains; cutting long and patching short, it amounted to seven thousand square.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: Yu delineated the Nine Provinces; Zhou divided the Six Domains—trimming long and patching short, the realm measured seven thousand square li.

sentences.zh: 國賦之所均，王教之所備，此謂華夏者也。

translations.literal: Where state levies were apportioned and royal instruction was provided—this is what is called Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: Where state levies were apportioned and royal instruction applied—this was Huaxia.

sentences.zh: 以圓蓋方輿之廣，廣谷大川之多，民生其間，胡可勝道，此謂蕃國者也。

translations.literal: Considering the breadth of the round canopy and square earth, the multitude of broad valleys and great rivers, and the people living among them—how could they all be told? This is what is called the barbarian states.
translations.idiomatic: Given the vastness of heaven and earth, the multitude of valleys and great rivers, and the peoples living among them beyond numbering—this is the barbarian world.

sentences.zh: 西南之蠻夷不少矣，雖言語不通，嗜欲不同，亦能候律瞻風，遠修職貢。

translations.literal: The Man and Yi of the southwest are not few; though languages do not communicate and desires differ, they also can observe the pitch pipes and watch the winds, and from afar cultivate duty and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The southwestern tribes are many; though their languages differ and their desires vary, they too can observe the seasons and winds and send tribute from afar.

sentences.zh: 但患己之不德，不患人之不來。

translations.literal: One need only worry about one's own lack of virtue, not worry that others will not come.
translations.idiomatic: The concern should be one's own lack of virtue, not whether others will come.

sentences.zh: 何以驗之？

translations.literal: How may this be verified?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be verified?

sentences.zh: 貞觀、開元之盛，來朝者多也！

translations.literal: In the prosperity of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan, those coming to court were many!
translations.idiomatic: In the prosperity of Zhenguan and Kaiyuan, how many came to court!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：五方異氣，所稟不同。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The five directions have different vapors; what they receive is not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: The five directions breathe different airs and receive different endowments.

sentences.zh: 維南極海，曰蠻與戎。

translations.literal: Only the south reaches the sea—called Man and Rong.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lies the ocean, home to Man and Rong.

sentences.zh: 惡我則叛，好我則通。

translations.literal: If they hate us they rebel; if they favor us they communicate.
translations.idiomatic: Those who resent us rebel; those who favor us come.

sentences.zh: 不可不德，使其瞻風。

translations.literal: One cannot fail to be virtuous and make them watch the winds.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue cannot be neglected if they are to turn toward our transforming influence.
